articles.title: Ozone hole largest in a decade — yet world remains on track to shrinking it
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The ozone hole covered 27.3 million sq. km on September 20. However, the levels of substances that harm the ozone layer have been coming down thanks to the Montreal Protocol

The European Space Agency (ESA) has said that the ozone hole over Antarctica this year is among the largest since scientists began monitoring it from space nearly five decades ago. The announcement, reported on November 26, is a reversal of fortune from 2025 — when the ozone hole was among the smallest in more than three decades. However, scientists reiterated that the hole naturally changes in size every year and that the world is still on course to shrinking it.

According to data from Copernicus — the European Union programme that monitors environmental conditions using satellites and ground-based instruments — the ozone hole covered 27.3 million sq. km on September 20, around 31% larger than the average for this time of year in the last two decades. On November 4, NASA and the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) had also reported that the hole was the seventh largest it has been on record between September 7 and October 13, at 25 million sq. km on average.

The ozone layer is around 15-35 km above the earth’s surface, in the stratosphere. The layer is named for its relatively high concentration of ozone, a molecule consisting of three oxygen atoms. This molecule absorbs much of the ultraviolet radiation coming from the sun, shielding organisms on the surface from its harmful effects.

In 1985, British Antarctic Survey scientists reported that the amount of ozone in the atmosphere above Antarctica declined seasonally. Scientists subsequently found the culprit to be compounds called chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), then widely used in refrigerators and industrial processes. When CFCs reach the stratosphere, ultraviolet radiation in sunlight breaks them apart and releases chlorine atoms. These atoms participate in chemical reactions that destroy ozone while also regenerating the chlorine atoms. In other words, once these reactions begin with a few chlorine atoms, they can destroy thousands of ozone molecules.

During winter in the southern hemisphere, strong winds circulating around Antarctica form the so-called polar vortex, which prevents the relatively warmer air between the continent and the equator from pushing in. Below certain temperatures, chemical reactions on the surfaces of particles in clouds convert chlorine compounds into forms that can rapidly destroy ozone when sunlight returns in the spring, i.e. September to November.

articles.title: Fair play: on a hurried delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The government must build consensus on delimitation

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) appears to have zeroed in on a hurried delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies as the central piece of its strategy for the next general election, due in 2029. As the current constitutional scheme stands, a fresh delimitation is triggered once the data from the ongoing Census 2027 is published . That default path, which is based on population distribution across States, will considerably cut down the representation of States that have stabilised their population since the last delimitation. The Centre has now proposed to extend the constitutional freeze on inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, while increasing the size of the House to a maximum of 850 seats. The demarcation of the boundaries of Lok Sabha constituencies will be based on the 2011 Census within each State. The delimitation exercise will also bring into force 33% reservation for women , which Parliament approved in 2023. Considering the need to balance the ‘one person, one vote’ principle with the principles of federalism, which is about protecting the group rights of States, the proposals are a reasonable way forward for India. That said, the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats is such a central question of democracy and federalism that any changes must be preceded by thoughtful deliberations at multiple levels.

That makes the approach of the Centre , which is trying to pass a constitutional amendment through defections and manipulations, dubious and lacking in good faith. If the Centre has been willing to extend the constitutional guarantee of inter-State distribution of seats on the basis of the 1971 Census, it could have built an all-party consensus on the issue . Instead, in April, it made a deceptive move by promising to maintain the current proportion of seats while the constitutional amendment it moved would have made that promise unconstitutional. At present, when the Centre is keen to appear accommodative, a more appropriate manner to proceed with such a generational measure in India’s federal democracy is to refer the Bills to a parliamentary committee that can examine them in detail and generate a national conversation. A bigger Lok Sabha will create its own challenges , while the case for increasing its size is not entirely without merit as India’s population has grown by at least 2.6 times since the 1971 Census, which forms the basis of the last delimitation of 1973, based on the 1971 Census. The Centre should not rush this vital question, which is not merely about garnering enough votes for passing a Bill. It must be based on consensus, as it happened in 1976 and again in 2001, under a Prime Minister from the Congress and one from the BJP, respectively.

articles.title: Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance.

The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 28 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance.

The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

articles.title: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN

Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke.
E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.
Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

articles.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh arrested on charges of harassing IAS officer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TVK MLA was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed
A case was registered after the Madras High Court recently directed the State Public Prosecutor to get in touch with the officer regarding the allegations after she filed a formal police complaint .

Police sources said a team led by Shristi Singh, the Investigating Officer appointed by the Madras High Court , arrested the legislator at his residence in Kallakurichi on Friday evening and took him in a police vehicle. He was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed.

The Kallakurichi All Women Police, which had registered a sexual harassment case against the MLA, served summons on Mr. Vignesh on Wednesday directing him to appear for questioning in connection with the case. Speculation over his arrest grew after Inspector Bhuvaneshwari, attached to the All Women Police station, visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi on Wednesday (November 25) and handed the summons to him in person .

On 23.11.2026, a senior lady officer in Kallakurichi District preferred complaint against Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency regarding alleged harassment and inappropriate conduct. On the same day, a case in Kallakurichi AWPS Cr No. 91/2026 was registered under appropriate sections of law. Initial investigation was done by the local police and on the directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras in WP (Crl) No. 3183/2026 dated 24.11.2026, Tmt. Shristi Singh, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Tiruppur District took investigation of this case under the supervision of Tmt. N. Kamini, IPS, Inspector General of Police, Administration, Chennai. During the investigation, the petitioner and other witnesses have been enquired by the Investigation Officer. Consequent to the enquiry, the alleged accused Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency has been arrested and the investigation is under progress. Relating to this incident, 201 social media posts were pulled down by the local police and the Cyber Crime Department of Tamil Nadu Police. However, since the Hon'ble High Court has also ordered against publishing, communicating or making known to the public any of the matters covered under sections PoSH Act, it is requested to avoid posting any post in contravention to the above directions..
The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Ms. Singh began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station.

Watch: Vijay promised women’s safety. Did his government deliver? | Focus Tamil Nadu
Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini also visited Kallakurichi on Thursday (November 26) and supervised the investigation.

The opposition DMK, AIADMK, PMK and BJP had demanded his arrest after the incident came to light. The BJP Mahila Morcha also held Statewide protests on Friday (November 27), accusing the government of shielding the MLA.

The local police and the Cyber Crime Department had taken down 201 social media posts related to the incident, according to the police. The High Court has barred publishing, communicating or making public any matter covered under the PoSH Act, it said, urging the public not to post anything that violates these directions.

articles.title: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri appointed as J&K’s Advocate General after two year gap
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Faisal is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice; the Omar Abdullah government in April had proposed the names for the post while the appointment came after the J&K High Court heard a PIL plea on November 5 regarding the vacant post

Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was on Friday (November 27, 2026) appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir, eight months after the J&K government forwarded the proposal to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for his approval. The J&K government has been without an Advocate General for more than two years.

“In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 79 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (Act No. 34 of 2019) and in supersession of notification S.O. No. 07 of 2019 dated 01-11-2019, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is pleased to appoint Mr. Syed Faisal Qadri, Senior Advocate, as Advocate General for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir,” reads the official order.

Mr. Qadri is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice. With over 100 reported judgments, Mr. Faisal earned a name for himself by pleading cases of both private and government institutions in the J&K High Court and in the Supreme Court.

The Omar Abdullah government in April this year had proposed the names for the post. The appointment, however, came after the J&K High Court heard a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on November 5 regarding the vacant post. Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli had apprised the Division Bench, comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajnesh Oswal, that the appointment would be made within a period of one month.

It is a major relief for Chief Minister Omar Abdullah whose government was pursuing many pending policy matters before the J&K High Court in the past two years. Mr. Abdullah’s party National Conference (NC) had won the Assembly elections in 2024, but remained without an Advocate General since then.
In 2019, senior advocate D.C. Raina was appointed as the Advocate General of J&K. He, later, tendered his resignation in October 2024.

The Omar Abdullah government in April this year had proposed the names for the post. The appointment, however, came after the J&K High Court heard a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on November 5 regarding the vacant post. In 2019, senior advocate D.C. Raina was appointed as the Advocate General of J&K. He, later, tendered his resignation in October 2024.

articles.title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The new Constitutional Amendment Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%; they also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha

A new Constitutional Amendment Bill approved by the Union Cabinet on Friday (November 27, 2026) proposes an extension of the existing freeze on the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, addressing the core concern of States that feared a loss of their proportionate strength due to the decline in their share of the national population.

The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population.

The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution. The guarantee for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for each State is being written into this, providing that, for the purposes of giving immediate effect to such reservation for women, “the delimitation so undertaken shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats allocated to each State and Union territory in the House of the People.” The total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State and Union territory will also increase similarly, “over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation”.

The new Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%, while the maximum strength of the lower House will rise from the current 550 to 850. If these Bills are passed by Parliament in its special sittings from November 30 to December 3, the path to immediate delimitation will open, which will also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
ALSO WATCH Cabinet clears delimitation Bill; is a two-thirds majority within reach? | Above the Fold | Nov 27, 2026

Amendments to Articles 81 and 82, which mandate the size and distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the States, propose to extend a sunset clause for the existing proportion until the first Census after 2051.

The existing provision in Article 82 that says that “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, it shall not be necessary to readjust” the distribution of seats is being amended in the Bill and will be changed to read “until the year 2051”.

Article 82 currently has two definitions for population: for the purposes of distribution among States, the 1971 population; and for the purposes of delimitation of individual constituencies within the States, the 2001 Census. The proposed amendment will extend the sunset clause to “until the year 2051”, but the reference to the 1971 Census has been dropped.

The Bill proposes that the distribution among States will be determined “in accordance with Article 334A”, while the boundaries of individual constituencies will be determined by the “latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026”.

articles.title: Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The distribution of seats based on 1971 Census continued for 50 years for the reason that a readjustment would adversely affect the proportion of States that stabilised population. Population stability was a stated objective of the government. That link between population stability and Lok Sabha share has been removed in the 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill

The amendments in the Constitution being proposed in a Bill approved by the Union Cabinet propose to continue the existing proportion of strength in the Lok Sabha of individual States for another 25 years, until 2051.

The existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats was based on the population distribution recorded in the 1971 Census, and determined in the delimitation of 1973. That distribution continued for 50 years for the reason that a readjustment would adversely affect the proportion of States that stabilised population. Population stability was a stated objective of the Indian government. That link between population stability and Lok Sabha share has been removed in the proposed 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill. The freeze on proportion will continue for another 25 years, as a special measure to accommodate 33 per cent seats for women.

articles.title: Navy Project 17A programme completed as GRSE hands over final stealth frigate Vindhyagir
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024) is the third and final Project 17A frigate built by GRSE

The Indian Navy on Friday (November 27, 2026) received Vindhyagiri, the seventh and final ship of the Nilgiri-class (Project 17A) stealth frigates, from Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd (GRSE) in Kolkata, marking the completion of the Project 17A ship delivery programme and a significant milestone in India’s indigenous warship construction capabilities.

Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024) is the third and final Project 17A frigate built by GRSE. With its delivery on Friday (November 27, 2026), all seven ships under the programme have been handed over to the Navy within 23 months of the delivery of the first ship, INS Nilgiri, on December 20, 2024, the Defence Ministry said.

Designed by the Navy’s Warship Design Bureau and overseen by the Warship Overseeing Team in Kolkata, the Project 17A frigates represent a generational leap in indigenous warship design, stealth, survivability and combat capabilities.

The multi-mission platforms are equipped with an advanced suite of weapons and sensors, enhancing their capabilities across anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine warfare domains. They also feature Combined Diesel or Gas (CODOG) propulsion systems, comprising a diesel engine and a gas turbine, along with an Integrated Platform Management System.

The construction period of Vindhyagiri was reduced to 68 months, compared with 84 months taken for the first-of-class INS Nilgiri, reflecting the experience gained during the construction of the preceding six ships.

Named after the Vindhyagiri mountain range in Karnataka, the frigate is a reincarnation of the erstwhile INS Vindhyagiri, a Leander-class frigate that served the Navy for 31 years, from July 8, 1981, to June 11, 2012.

With an indigenous content of 75%, the Project 17A programme involved more than 200 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It generated employment for approximately 4,000 personnel directly and over 10,000 indirectly.
The delivery underscores the Navy’s focus on Aatmanirbharta in warship design and construction, while highlighting the country’s growing capabilities in complex naval shipbuilding.

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.
High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. .
Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article.

Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18.
“The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out.
Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October.

Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick.

Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased.

On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said.

Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.
“The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.
“Strong bank and non-bank credit growth continues to support the domestic economy. Further, sustained double-digit export growth broadened the base of economic expansion,” they added.
Equity markets remained buoyant amid robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio investment inflows, while net inflows through external commercial borrowings and NRI deposits remained strong.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.
September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.
Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.
Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday.

A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market.

The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun.

The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: U.S. disables ship trying to leave Iran, as Tehran vows to confront blockade
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to ⁠Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said: “Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be ‌reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place,” Iranian state media reported

The U.S. military said on Friday (November 27, 2026) ‌it disabled a commercial ship on Thursday (November 26, 2026) ​after it attempted to ⁠run the US blockade of Iran, while an adviser to the Iranian supreme leader ‌said Iran would keep the Strait of Hormuz shut ‌while vowing to break the embargo.

CENTCOM disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, Nov. 26, after the crew attempted to run the U.S. naval blockade, despite multiple warnings, following departure from Bandar Abbas. A U.S. military aircraft launched precision munitions that struck the stern of Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer. The ship's propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed. Read the full release online: https://t.co/4CAaN4gDvW

The ‌U.S. ⁠Central Command said in ⁠a statement that military aircraft launched precision munitions that struck the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V ​Pacific Archer ‌in the Gulf of Oman after it departed from the Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas, and ‌the ship’s propulsion was disabled while ​the civilian crew was unharmed.

Meanwhile, Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to ⁠Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said: “Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be ‌reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place,” Iranian state media reported. He did not give details of Iran’s plans for breaking the embargo.

The U.S. ‌reimposed its naval blockade on Iranian ports ​in July, and earlier this month announced Task Force Iron ⁠Gate to restrict the movement of weapons ⁠and sanctioned materials across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian ‌Sea.

articles.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from ‌Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising ​costs eroded the country’s competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh’s economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped ‌make Bangladesh the world’s second apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more ‌than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.
India has emerged ‌as ⁠the biggest beneficiary, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery ⁠reliability, industry leaders said.
Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest rise in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers’ demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, ​said the wage increase was “satisfactory” and that he hoped all ‌workers would resume work from Saturday.
Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh’s labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards.
Babul Akhter, a union leader and workers’ representative on the government-appointed wage board, said brands should not use the unrest to justify shifting orders out of Bangladesh.

He said retailers already factor political instability and labour ‌unrest into sourcing decisions, making such moves “hard to justify” and raising “serious doubts” whether the unrest was more than an excuse.

Factory ​owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of ⁠the business.
Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Accused shot during exchange of fire with police West Bengal’s Asansol
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused

An accused wanted in multiple cases in West Bengal’s Asansol, was on Friday (November 27, 2026) shot in his right leg during an alleged clash leading to an exchange of fire with the police when they went to arrest him on Friday morning. The accused, Pratap Das, is wanted in several cases of robbery, theft, iron smuggling, and cyber fraud across Asansol. Police have been searching for him for the past few days in connection with a cyber fraud case lodged last week at Asansol South Police Station. When the police went to arrest him on Friday (November 27, 2026) from a hideout in the Ismail area, he opened fire at the police team. Later, he was shot in retaliatory fire.
According to the police, an operation to arrest Pratap was launched on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) when he again opened fire at the police team upon spotting them and managed to flee.

The operation was launched by the Asansol Durgapur Police Commissionerate Special Operations Group (SOG), along with officers from Hirapur police station, following a tip-off that he was hiding in the area and carrying a firearm. The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused.

Shots of firing were heard in broad daylight causing panic among residents who witnessed a cat and mouse chase between the accused and police. The accused was seen being dragged from one of the houses out by the police with blood dripping from his right leg and was carried on all fours to a police vehicle.

Local residents in the area said that they had no idea about the accused. “We did not know that he was hiding in our neighbourhood. I went to drop my daughter off at school when I saw police chasing him. It was scary,” said a woman who stays in the area from where Pratap was arrested.

Association for Protection of Democratic Reforms, a civil rights group raised questions about the manner in which police paraded in groups with weapons. “Instead of relying on intelligence inputs, a scientific approach, and proper procedures to apprehend the criminal, the police’s actual objective was to intimidate the general public through a display of firepower,” APDR vice president Ranajit Sur said.

The development comes after a total of five encounters that took place in West Bengal since the new Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power. Five people who have been shot dead by the police during these incidents include three accused in rape cases of minors and two accused of murder.

articles.title: Not a single foot of blacktopping done on Amarnath route, PDP-BJP stoking Hindu-Muslim discord: Omar Abdullah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route,’ said Omar Abdullah

J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday (November 27, 2026) said not a single foot of blacktopping was carried out on the Amarnath route, while referring to the Sheshnag controversy, and accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) of “deliberately pitting Hindus and Muslims against each other”.

“The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot [referring to the PDP] are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route. They are alleging macadamisation. I challenge them to prove a single foot of blacktopping done on the route. I am ready to face an inquiry. There is a court [Supreme Court] direction to have a 12-feet stretch,” said Mr. Abdullah.

Mr. Abdullah’s statement came days after local parties, religious leaders, environmentalists and civil society bodies reacted sharply to the presence of an earthmover close functioning to the Sheshnag lake situation at an altitude of 11,780 feet on the way to the Amarnath shrine, which is around 20 km away from the spot.

A report prepared by the J&K Forest Department on the viral video, in which an earthmover was seen close to the lake, said, “The activity seen in the video is part of routine annual maintenance operations being undertaken by the Border Roads Organisation [BRO]. No new road construction or fresh alignment is being undertaken.

It is further clarified that the Yatra track runs along the right-hand side of the lake and is situated at a considerable distance from the lake. “It said the lake remains protected and the maintenance activity in question “was not intended to alter its character or ecological integrity”.

“The matter may, therefore, be viewed in its proper context, keeping in view the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the safety requirements of the annual pilgrimage and the longstanding nature of the track maintenance operations,” it added, while underlining that the maintenance and improvement of this track is a longstanding exercise undertaken regularly since 2012 and “not a new activity initiated in 2026”.

However, Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti, who was denied permission to visit the spot with police citing security concerns, has asked the government to allow a team of politicians and experts to visit the Sheshnag lake.

“If the Union Territory [UT] government is relying on satellite images to claim that no construction is taking place at Sheshnag, why not allow us to visit the site and see for ourselves? The JCBs wreaking havoc there are visible for all to see. To dispel all doubts, let the Chief Minister depute a team of political leaders and environmentalists to inspect the site and establish the truth. What is there to hide?” said Ms. Mufti.

Meanwhile, referring to the allegations of irregularities in the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination conducted by the J&K Service Selection Board JKSSB), Mr. Abdullah said, “Political opponents were exploiting the concerns of unemployed youth and creating unnecessary mistrust about the recruitment process. I am always ready to admit if a mistake is committed. But when I dug deep into the matter, I found that instead of there being fraud in the examination, the fact is that the system worked properly. The paper did not leak. The paper was not stolen.”

Terming the incident as a case of “attempted cheating but disallowed”, Mr. Abdullah said, “There were people who tried to cheat in the examination. I agree with this. They took out the question paper from the examination hall, used wireless devices and tried to get answers. But they were caught on the spot. They were arrested. The JKSSB should have been praised for it,” said Mr. Abdullah.
Meanwhile, protests in J&K over the JKSSB recruitments continued with protesters demanding postponement of the upcoming examination for the posts of Sub-Inspector “till reformations are carried out”.
The JKSSB had conducted the Finance Accounts Assistant examination on November 15, 2026, for around 600 posts and around 1,62 lakh candidates appear in it.

articles.title: In Kolkata, the BJP redraws power lines
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP government in West Bengal has taken up a delimitation exercise of civic bodies of the twin cities of Kolkata and Howrah, increasing the number of wards in both municipal corporations. Opposition parties have claimed there has been gerrymandering. Elections will impact over seven million people. Shrabana Chatterjee and Shiv Sahay Singh examine the delimitation exercise and the related legal challenges

Before August 2026, the erstwhile ward number 58 of Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), located in central-east Kolkata’s Topsia area resembled a contiguous irregular polygon. After the delimitation of KMC wards, the areas under ward 58 have been split into three: 73, 74, and 75. The newly demarcated ward number 73, now somewhat resembles a hammer, with a narrow strip of land connecting two areas.

The delimitation exercise, now challenged in the Supreme Court of India, has been coupled with accusations of gerrymandering. Gerrymandering, a two-century-old political tool, is defined as the practice of drawing the boundaries of electoral constituencies in a way that gives one political party, or group, or individual an unfair advantage over others.

Three months after coming to power in West Bengal in the summer of 2026, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government, on August 12, passed The Kolkata Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the State Assembly. Its provisions increased the number of wards of the city’s civic body from 144 to 209.

While the last delimitation of wards of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation was carried out in 1980, during the time of the Left Front government, almost 46 years ago, Opposition members say that the BJP has now carved out wards to benefit themselves, in the local body elections.

Sajal Ghosh, former councillor of the previous ward no. 50 and BJP MLA of Kolkata’s Baranagar Assembly seat, says a delimitation was necessary. “The municipal corporation is like a service industry. In your lifetime you may or may not need an MLA. One in 10,000 may need an MP, but there is no family who does not require the services of their councillor and the municipality where they stay,” he adds.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh Khadi Mahotsav begins in Lucknow
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Based on the theme ‘Culture in Threads, Progress through Khadi’, a total of 150 stalls have been set up at the festival by Khadi and Village Industries entrepreneurs and artisans from various districts of the State,’ said Rakesh Sachan

Uttar Pradesh Minister for Khadi and Village Industries, Silk Industry and MSME Rakesh Sachan in Lucknow on Friday (November 27, 2026) said Khadi is not merely a fabric, but a powerful idea of self-respect, Swadeshi and self-reliance. Mr. Sachan made the remark while inaugurating the 10-day state-level ‘Uttar Pradesh Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ on Friday at the Central Sanskrit University campus in Lucknow’s Gomti Nagar. Organized by the Uttar Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board, the festival will run from 27 November to 06 December 2026. “The Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, had made Khadi the most important medium in the struggle for the country’s independence and self-reliance. The Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s calls for ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ have given Khadi a new identity and fresh momentum since 2014, “ said the Minister.

Minister Rakesh Sachan said that under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the State government is committed to creating employment in rural areas and making young people ‘not job seekers, but job creators’. He said that over the past 05 years, loans worth ₹2,544.35 crore have been disbursed under the ‘Chief Minister’s Village Industries Employment Scheme’ and the ‘Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme’. With this financial assistance, 24,799 village industries units have been established across the state, providing direct employment to more than 2,79,000 people. In addition, through 27,508 stalls at 115 exhibitions organized in all 18 divisions of the state, entrepreneurs have recorded sales of more than ₹161.54 crore, reflecting the growing public confidence in Khadi and Village Industries products.

Mr. Sachan said that by adopting Khadi garments for weddings and other auspicious occasions, citizens are enriching traditional culture. “New Khadi sales centers are being opened in various cities for the convenience of customers. In addition, a special discount of 30% is being offered on the purchase of Khadi fabrics and garments from Gandhi Jayanti [02 October], so that more and more people can connect with Swadeshi products. Based on the theme ‘Culture in Threads, Progress through Khadi’, a total of 150 stalls have been set up at the festival by Khadi and Village Industries entrepreneurs and artisans from various districts of the State,” said the Minister.

Mr. Sachan also visited all the stalls and encouraged the artisans. He said that today’s Khadi, with the assurance of 100 percent pure cotton, is increasingly becoming the first choice of young people in the form of modern and designer garments. Principal Secretary, Khadi and Village Industries Department, Anil Kumar Sagar, and Chief Executive Officer of the U.P. Khadi and Village Industries Board, Shishir, were present at the inaugural ceremony.

articles.title: Makkah alliance countries review regional security situation, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘The committee reviewed the evolving regional security situation and reaffirmed the determination of the three countries to continue working collectively towards peace, security, and stability,’ said Ishaq Dar

The top officials of the trilateral Makkah Defence Alliance on Friday (November 27, 2026) met in Pakistan's capital and reviewed the evolving regional security situation while condemning "persistent and heinous" attacks by Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi militia on Saudi Arabia.
Comment | A new security triangle emerges with the Makkah Pact

The Makkah defence agreement , signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August, establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of them would be regarded as an attack against all.

The meeting of the third session of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) — the highest decision-making body of the alliance — was held in Islamabad, which was decorated with the flags of Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Addressing the media after the meeting, which lasted for more than two hours, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that the three countries reiterated their commitment to the pact, including collective defence, mutual solidarity and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, Dawn reported.

“The committee reviewed the evolving regional security situation and reaffirmed the determination of the three countries to continue working collectively towards peace, security, and stability,” he said.
He said the committee also reviewed progress towards implementing the decisions taken at the previous meeting of the Makkah Alliance for Defence.
The two previous meetings of the committee — which comprises the foreign and defence ministers and top military officials of the three countries — were held in Istanbul and Riyadh.

Mr. Dar said the three countries agreed to continue consultations to enhance cooperation and coordination among them in areas of mutual interest, and to support efforts towards de-escalation of regional tensions and encourage peaceful dispute resolution.

The three countries condemned the “persistent and heinous” attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their “collective resolve” to continue efforts in safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity in accordance with the “collective defence provisions” in the pact, Mr. Dar said.

He said that the three countries also pledged to strengthen cooperation in defence industries, joint technological development, training and capacity building “with a view to enhancing the collective capabilities and cohesion of their armed forces in order to address mutual security concerns and contribute to peace and security in the region.”
Earlier, a senior official in the Shehbaz Sharif government told PTI that the Foreign and Defence Ministers as well as senior military leaders from the three countries attended the meeting.

articles.title: Hamas says Israel tried to kill chief’s son in Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘Izz al-Din al-Hayya, the youngest surviving son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, along with his family and the family of his late brother Azzam, survived an Israeli assassination attempt,’ a security source in Gaza told AFP

Hamas said Israel tried to kill an adult son of the Palestinian movement's chief, Khalil al-Hayya, in an overnight strike on Friday (November 27, 2026), with a Gaza security source telling AFP he survived.
Editorial | Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
The strike follows a series of killings by the Israeli military in recent days that have targeted Hamas officials, despite a ceasefire in the war-shattered Palestinian territory.
Separately, Gaza's civil defence agency said Israeli forces killed seven people across the territory on Friday (November 27).

"Izz al-Din al-Hayya, the youngest surviving son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, along with his family and the family of his late brother Azzam, survived an Israeli assassination attempt early on Friday targeting a residential apartment in the Rimal neighbourhood, west of Gaza City," a security source in Gaza told AFP .
When asked by AFP , the Israeli military said it was looking into the incident.

Bassem Naim, a member of the Palestinian Islamist movement's political bureau, told AFP that "Israel's attempt to target the youngest son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya... constitutes 'state terrorism,'" while Hamas issued a statement calling the targeting "cowardly".
Four of Mr. al-Hayya's sons have already been killed in Israeli attacks, including one in May and another in an Israeli strike targeting Hamas leaders in Doha in September 2025.

Gaza's civil defence agency, a rescue force which operates under Hamas authority, said an Israeli drone strike west of Rafah city in southern Gaza killed three people on Friday (November 27), with nearby Nasser Hospital confirming it received three bodies following the strike.
The Israeli military told AFP it had struck "three terrorists in the area".
Another drone strike west of Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza killed one person, the civil defence and Al-Shifa Hospital said.
The Israeli military said it was checking the incident.

articles.title: Holy Family Hospital opens 150-bed super speciality block in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the facility at the hospital premises on Okhla Road

Holy Family Hospital in south Delhi on Friday inaugurated a 150-bed super speciality block, expanding its capacity to provide advanced cancer care, organ transplantation and specialised neurological and cardiac services.

Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the facility at the hospital premises on Okhla Road. The new block will introduce services in surgical, radiation and medical oncology, haematology-oncology and bone marrow transplantation, nuclear medicine, advanced cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, neurology and neurosurgery, and organ transplantation.
The expansion takes the hospital’s total bed capacity from 345 to 495, strengthening its ability to treat patients requiring complex and critical medical interventions.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Radhakrishnan called for cancer institutions across the country, including Holy Family Hospital, to establish a common forum to share expertise, discuss challenges in oncology and work towards making quality cancer treatment more accessible and affordable.

The inauguration carried historical significance for the institution. Archbishop Anil J.T. Couto, president of the New Delhi Holy Family Hospital Society, recalled that the foundation stone of the original hospital building was laid in 1953 by the then Vice-President, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. Seventy-three years later, another Vice-President bearing the same surname inaugurated its new super speciality facility.

A message from Pope Leo XIV congratulating the hospital was read out by Andrea Francia, Chargé d’Affaires at the Apostolic Nunciature in India. The Pope described the new facility as a manifestation of the Church’s continuing commitment to the healing mission of Jesus Christ.

Established in 1953 by the Medical Mission Sisters, Holy Family Hospital is a charitable, non-profit institution managed by the Delhi Catholic Archdiocese. The NABH- and NABL-accredited hospital says the new block will combine advanced medical technology and specialist expertise with its commitment to providing affordable healthcare across socio-economic groups.(EOM)

articles.title: Methil Radhakrishnan receives Ezhuthachan Award, Keralam’s highest literary honour
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Methil Radhakrishnan is an original writer, says Keralam CM Satheesan while presenting Ezhuthachan Award to Radhakrishnan in Kozhikode
Methil Radhakrishnan introduced an experimental form of writing in Malayalam by easily blending science and philosophy with literature, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has said.

He was delivering a speech after presenting Ezhuthachan Award, the highest literary honour given by the Kerala government, to Mr. Radhakrishnan at the Kozhikode Town Hall here on Saturday (November 28, 2026).
Mr. Satheesan said that Mr. Radhakrishnan style of writing and presentation of language were original and thus different from others.

“Bringing in science and philosophy in literature was considered a difficult proposition earlier. Mr. Radhakrishnan, one of the torch-bearers of post-modernism in Malayalam literature, proved that it was possible without the reader even noticing the process,” the Chief Minister said, adding that Mr. Radhakrishnan had also been a keen observer of nature, unlike many others, which get reflected in his writing as well.
“The literary works of very few writers merit a re-reading. Mr. Radhakrishnan is one among them,” Mr. Satheesan pointed out.
Kalpetta Narayanan, writer, described Mr. Radhakrishnan as someone who walked much ahead of his times, while deeply engaging with multiple subjects in his writing.

Describing Ezhuthachan as a modern writer, Mr. Radhakrishnan said in his acceptance speech that the father of modern Malayalam language had been a formative influence in his literary career. Each letter in Ezhuchachan’s Harinamakeerthanam described a different human experience, Mr. Radhakrishnan said.

Writer Sara Joseph, Minister for Cultural Affairs P.C. Vishnunadh, Kozhikode MP M.K. Raghavan, MLAs K. Praveenkumar and K. Jayanth, K. Gopalakrishnan, Special Secretary (Cultural Affairs), and District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty, among others, were present.

The annual award, the highest literary honour in Keralam, is named after Thunchaththu Ezhuthachan, believed to be the father of modern Malayalam language. It comes with a ₹5 lakh reward and a citation.

articles.title: Former High Court judges review arrangements at Thirupparankundram ahead of ‘Deepathoon’ lamp lighting; CRPF takes over security
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: After a closed-door meeting with priests, HR&CE officials, the Collector and CRPF officers, central forces took over security at the foothills and the contested ‘Deepathoon’ site

Two former Madras High Court judges, S. Vaidyanathan and V. Parthiban, visited the Sri Subramaniaswamy Temple here on Saturday (November 28, 2026) to assess the prevailing ground situation and review administrative arrangements around the Thirupparankundram hill.

After a brief inspection of the temple precincts, the judges chaired a consultative meeting with the temple priests (bhattars), senior Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) officials, District Collector Nishant Krishna and senior officials of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF).

During the closed-door deliberations, the judges sought detailed briefings from the bhattars on the traditional rituals and customary practices associated with the shrine and the hilltop. Temple administrators and the Collector apprised the judges of the measures in place to regulate the movement of crowds and maintain public order.
The judges emphasised the need for strict adherence to established legal frameworks, while ensuring that routine religious observances proceed without disruption.
After the review, CRPF personnel formally took over security responsibilities at the foothills and around the contested Deepathoon site.
Meanwhile, a group of devotees and members of Hindu outfits tried to cross police barricades to climb the hill towards the Deepathoon pillar.

Armed CRPF contingents have since set up a multi-tiered security cordon along the trekking paths and entry points leading up the Thirupparankundram hill, in coordination with the local police and the district administration.
Essentials such as oil, a bowl and other materials were also taken to the Deepathoon site.

articles.title: Mission Chakkakompan: Coexistence Collective slams operation to radio-collar problem tusker, demands probe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Coexistence Collective, a coalition of environmental organisations and civil society groups, has accused the Keralam Forest Department of leading a “cruel persecution” of the wild tusker ‘Chakkakompan’ over the past three days in Chinnakanal, Idukki district.

The collective has demanded stringent action against all persons led by the Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF) who undertook the “illegal” action against the elephant in violation of international treaties and the guidelines and standard operating procedures (SOP) of the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF).

The Collective also urged the authorities to drop the plan to fit a radio collar on the tusker as it was “completely unnecessary.” The forum said it has written to Union Minister of Forests Bhupendra Yadav, the MoEF, Project Elephant, Keralam’s Forest Minister Shibu Baby John, Principal Secretary (Forests) and the Chief Wildlife Warden.

The State Forest department had on Friday evening temporarily suspended the mission to fit a radio collar on the tusker after an attempt to sedate the elephant failed although it was shot with two tranquiliser darts. The Collective’s representatives including N. Badusha of Wayanad and M.N. Jayachandran from Idukki have also called for a comprehensive investigation into ‘Mission Chakkakompan,’ terming the Forest Department’s action an “unparalleled and cruel elephant hunt.”

Close to 150 people were hounding the tusker all over the place by shouting and bursting crackers. It is shameful that such “festivities” were conducted inside the forest. The Western Ghats regions of Keralam have transformed into a killing zone of elephants, the collective said in a statement, further alleging that more than 40 elephants have died under mysterious circumstances over the past five years.

The Collective said that a lobby that included the big resorts, quarries, settlers who encroach upon tribal lands and their “protectors” that include political and religious leaders were behind the operation to trap the elephant.

articles.title: Delimitation Bill LIVE: This Bill is dangerous to democracy, says Kharge; DMK announces support for Centre's proposal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Opposition leaders discuss a joint response ahead of special session; parties warn the move could distort representation, weaken federalism and politically benefit the BJP

The Centre made an oral assurance while introducing the Bill to increase Lok Sabha seats that each State’s share would increase by 50% on a pro-rata basis. However, the increase could weaken the Rajya Sabha’s role as a check on the lower House, while the Lok Sabha’s limited sitting days would leave MPs with less time to raise issues

​ Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051 Centre proposes 25-year freeze on inter-State Lok Sabha seat distribution, plus 50% seat rise and 33% women reservation by 2051. ​
Centre proposes 25-year freeze on inter-State Lok Sabha seat distribution, plus 50% seat rise and 33% women reservation by 2051.

In a social post in Hindi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah says, the Cabinet’s approval of the 132nd Constitution Amendment Bill is a major step toward increasing people’s representation in all states and bringing governance closer to the people.
He says the Bill will allow Uttar Pradesh to increase its representation in the Legislative Assembly without being divided, in addition to providing the one-third reservation for women.
All parties in Uttar Pradesh should welcome and support this historic bill, he says.
Questioning the hurry for the exercise when Census is underway, Mr. Kharge says if govt goes by latest census, SC/ST will get more seats, but they don’t want that.
INDIA bloc leaders believe Constitution amendment bill being brought by govt is dangerous for democracy, says Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.
Constitution amendment bill is aimed at finishing off democracy. This govt wants ‘800 paar’ to keep power in their hands permanently, he claims.
Former minister A.K. Saseendran said the decision to quit the NCP (SP) had been vindicated by the party’s decision to support the BJP-led central government on the proposed delimitation legislation.

Speaking to reporters about the NCP(SP)’s decision to support the proposed delimitation legislation, Mr. Saseendran said: “We have all been part of the Left Democratic Front’s politics since the 1980s. Unfortunately, the moves now being pursued from Delhi are not in keeping with that political ideology. We are therefore completely satisfied that the decision we took was right. We intend to move forward along that right path.”

A faction led by Mr. Saseendran and Thomas K Thomas had broken away from the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) in Keralam, to form NCP (Secular), which was subsequently merged with the LDF constituent Congress (Secular). The new party has approached the Election Commission seeking approval for the name Congress Socialist Party (CSP). - PTI

articles.title: INDIA bloc leaders meet at Kharge’s residence to discuss joint strategy ahead of Parliament’s special sitting
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kapil Sibal alleged that the government’s delimitation Bill is aimed at keeping the BJP in power for 30-40 years, as the Centre is set to introduce a fresh constitutional amendment Bill on Monday (November 30, 2026)

INDIA bloc floor leaders met at the residence of the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, on Saturday (November 28, 2026), and deliberated on a joint strategy in view of the government’s imminent move to reintroduce a constitutional amendment Bill in Parliament, involving delimitation.

Besides Congress president Mr. Kharge, former party chief Rahul Gandhi, Trinamool Congress (TMC)’s Abhishek Banerjee, Independent Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)’s Abhay Kumar Singh and Manoj Jha, Communist Party of India’s P. Sandosh Kumar, Indian Union Muslim League’s E.T. Mohammed Basheer, Revolutionary Socialist Party’s N.K. Premchandran, among others, took part in the meeting.

Congress general secretaries Jairam Ramesh, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K.C. Venugopal, among others, also attended. Non-INDIA bloc parties such as the DMK, the Aam Aadmi Party and the Biju Janata Dal were also invited but stayed away.

“Look, we need to examine this from the perspective of what is going to happen at the national level and what lies ahead. At the national level, if this Bill is passed, the number of Lok Sabha seats could increase to around 850. The first question is whether a House of 850 members can function properly,” Mr. Sibal told reporters ahead of the meeting.

“But the most serious issue is that their objective is not merely women’s reservation. We are ready for women’s reservation. They can implement it immediately within the existing 543 seats. So that is not their real objective. Their real objective is to remain in power for the next 30-40 years. And for that, what matters most to them is the Delimitation Bill,” he said.

“They will make appointments to the delimitation body in the same way they appointed Gyanesh Kumar to the Election Commission. In other words, another Gyanesh Kumar will be placed in this position. They will decide the boundaries of constituencies in states such as Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Maharashtra according to their own preferences,” he said.
Such manipulation is called gerrymandering, and by carrying out such gerrymandering, the BJP wanted to remain in power for the next 40 years, Mr. Sibal alleged.

“And after that, once they secure a two-thirds majority in Parliament, particularly if the strength of the House increases to 850 and they manage to get two-thirds of those seats, they will certainly change the Constitution,” he said.

A special sitting of Parliament has been convened from November 30, 2026. The Lok Sabha has been reconvened on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, 2026. The sittings will conclude on December 3, 2026, subject to exigencies of government business.

The Centre is set to introduce a fresh constitutional amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday (November 30, 2026), to roll out one-third reservation for women by increasing each State and Union Territory’s seat allocation in the House, and the strength of their legislative Assemblies, by 50%, and freeze the revised allocations and boundaries until 2051.

The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026 seeks to raise the House’s maximum strength to 850, with up to 815 members from States and 35 from Union Territories. It also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a State Assembly from 500 to 650.

The objective of the Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the States and the Union Territories, through a delimitation exercise, its Statement of Objects and Reasons says.

articles.title: Devotees gather at Thirupparankundram foothills under tight security
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two former Madras High Court judges, Justice S. Vaidyanathan and Justice V. Parthiban, who were appointed as receivers to oversee the temple’s affairs and ensure the ritual is conducted without obstruction, have already arrived in Madurai to supervise the arrangements

Scores of Hindu and Muslim devotees began arriving at the foothills of the Thirupparankundram hill early Saturday morning, November 28, following the Supreme Court’s directive permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam atop the ‘Deepathoon’ stone pillar.

Amid heightened security and coordinated crowd-management measures, worshippers gathered peacefully to ascend the hill to visit the Kasi Vishwanathar temple and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah.

In strict compliance with the apex court’s Friday (November 27) order, personnel from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) have taken over security and surveillance responsibilities across the hill.

The deployment comes after a Supreme Court bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi suspended the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple’s Board of Trustees, appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to oversee the ceremonial lighting, and entrusted the CRPF with securing both the temple and the dargah.

Two former Madras High Court judges, Justice S. Vaidyanathan and Justice V. Parthiban, who were appointed as receivers to oversee the temple’s affairs and ensure the ritual is conducted on Saturday (November 28) without obstruction, have already arrived in Madurai to supervise the arrangements.
The court also stipulated that the lamp be lit at least 50 metres away from the Sikandar Dargah to ensure that religious activities at both sites continue undisturbed.
Working alongside the central force at the base of the hill, the Tamil Nadu police have been stationed at entry points since dawn to register devotees before they begin their climb.

Police personnel are verifying details and maintaining logs for pilgrims heading to the Kasi Vishwanathar temple as well as visitors bound for the Sikandar Dargah, ensuring smooth movement along the hill pathways and preventing overcrowding at the summit.
After days of legal and administrative standoff over the site of the ceremonial lamp, the atmosphere at the foothills remained orderly on Saturday morning.
Devotees from Madurai and neighbouring districts queued up patiently at the registration desks before making their way up the steps under the watchful eyes of the CRPF guards and State police.

With judicial receivers supervising the arrangements and tight security in place, they aim to ensure that both the Karthigai Deepam ceremony and daily prayers at the dargah proceed smoothly throughout the day, stated authorities.
Senior officials said, CRPF personnel from nine units were on standby to carry out security duties.
