articles.title: Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Had they contested separately, the SAD and the BJP would likely have split the Opposition space, leaving the AAP and the Congress as the principal rivals; united, they have become serious contenders

articles.title: Blistering heat, soaring UV levels and high humidity keep Kerala on its toes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: IMD warns of above-average temperatures across State as sweltering, sultry conditions prevail; several places record alarming levels of UV radiation; urban heat island effect amplifies the conditions

Blistering heat, soaring ultraviolet (UV) levels, oppressive humidity amplified by rising heat index values, and the urban heat island effect are making life increasingly uncomfortable across Kerala during the peak of the summer with residents reporting unease amid the sweltering, sultry conditions, which are expected to persist until the first week of May.
Visual story: How this year’s El Niño hit India’s farms

Temperatures crossed the 40˚C mark twice last week in Palakkad and are now dangerously hovering around heatwave threshold levels at many stations across the State, especially in Punalur and Palakkad. Coastal regions in north Kerala, including Kannur and Kozhikode, have also been experiencing sultry conditions due to unusually high relative humidity in the air, which drives the ‘feels-like’ temperature dangerously high.

The latest weather bulletin issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Friday warned of above-average temperatures across the State. The agency has forecast maximum temperatures of around 40˚C at isolated places in Palakkad district, 39˚C in Kollam district, 38˚C in Kottayam district, 37˚C in Alappuzha, Pathanamthitta, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Kannur, and Kasaragod districts, and 36˚C in Thiruvananthapuram district (2 to 3˚C above normal) until April 19.

In addition, the rising mercury levels have put many regions in the State at high risk from UV rays, with several places recording alarming levels of radiation this season, according to Dr. M.G. Manoj, a scientist with the Advanced Centre for Atmospheric Radar Research (ACARR) at Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT).

Data recorded by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) show that UV Index (UVI) values of 8–9, classified as “very high,” pose significant risks of sunburn, skin damage, and eye problems, Mr. Manoj said. This rise in UV levels, coupled with the urban heat island (UHI) effect, which makes temperatures in densely populated cities as much as 2˚C higher than in rural areas, makes life more difficult in urban regions. Materials used in constructing buildings, roads, and roofs, such as concrete, asphalt (tar), and bricks do not transmit light and have higher heat capacity and thermal conductivity, driving the temperatures up in the urban areas, making hot and humid conditions uncomfortable during summer.

However, according to IMD sources, a heatwave is unlikely to occur in Kerala this year as a weak La Niña, a climate pattern characterised by colder-than-normal sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean, is prevailing. It is expected that by the end of this month, summer rainfall will increase, preventing temperatures from reaching heatwave levels like those experienced in Kerala in 2024 during the El Niño period, the opposite of La Niña, which suppresses rainfall and causes dryness in the Indian subcontinent.

For a heatwave to be declared, the maximum temperature should be 40°C or more (for plains), with a departure from normal of at least 4.5°C. For coastal regions, the maximum temperature should be greater than or equal to 37°C, with a departure from normal of 4.5°C. Additionally, such conditions must be recorded at least at two stations for two consecutive days, as stipulated by the IMD. This is unlikely under the present conditions, as departures from normal have mostly remained within the range of 1–3°C so far this season, according to scientists.

articles.title: NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day
A report filed by an amicus curiae appointed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has flagged multiple gaps in the management of solid and liquid waste in Keralam.

The deficiencies have been pointed out in the observation note dated November 24, 2026 submitted in the matter related to the compliance of Municipal Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 and other environmental issues in the State. The amicus curiae made the observations based on the affidavits and compliance reports submitted by the authorities.

The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day, it said.

The amicus curiae pointed out that inert waste is being used for land filling without safeguards. Quoting a report submitted by the Keralam government, the report said that about 404.8 tonnes per day of inert waste is used for filling up appropriate portions of hilly areas, stadiums, railway platforms, yards and road embankment formations. No register of sites, test reports or approvals is given. Given the State’s wetlands and landslide-prone slopes, this practice needs strict control, it suggested.

The report said that the action on the illegal drains discharging untreated sewage into streams and water bodies has been initiated in only four districts, including Kollam, Ernakulam, Alappuzha and Kottayam as per the affidavit submitted by the government. Of the 723 illegal outlets in the four districts, 671 are in Ernakulam alone.

The total quantity of processed and unprocessed legacy (old) waste has increased from 19.54 lakh metric tonnes in December 2025 to 19,6 lakh metric tonnes in July 2026. The gap in total sewage generated and treated is as high as 3901.2 million litres daily, indicative of a serious concern, it said.

The amicus curiae has suggested a sample-based functional audit of composting bins and biogas plants. The four regional plants for sanitary waste treatment should be commissioned by a fixed date. For inert and land filling, a register of every site where inert are used for filling be maintained and published, with test reports and approvals.
The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds and the sea.

articles.title: 34% monsoon deficit, bleak August outlook set alarm bells ringing in Kerala
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: By the end of July, Kerala received just 853.8 mm of rain, well below the normal 1,301.7 mm. This raises concerns of a potential drought, particularly if the monsoon remains weak in August and September. An impending El Niño threaten to further diminish rainfall prospects.

As the southwest monsoon has crossed the halfway mark, Kerala is staring at a bleak season, with rainfall recording a deficit of around 34% during the first two months of the four-month monsoon season. The first two months typically account for around 65% of the total seasonal rainfall. However, by the end of July, the State had received only 853.8 mm of rainfall against the normal 1,301.7 mm for the period, a deficit of 34%.
Visual story: How this year’s El Niño hit India’s farms

Adding to the concern, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast below-normal rainfall for Kerala in August, which typically receives an average of 445.2 mm of rainfall during a normal monsoon, followed by 271.7 mm in September. This means that only an exceptionally large surplus in August and September could offset the deficit recorded during the peak monsoon months of June and July.

If the latest forecast and prevailing synoptic conditions are any indication, the State appears to be heading towards a drought year, particularly if the monsoon remains weak in August and September. Global weather models and prevailing synoptic conditions are not favourable for any significant enhancement of rainfall over Kerala during August.

Speaking to The Hindu , Neetha K. Gopal, Director of the IMD, Thiruvananthapuram, said that after two days of moderate to heavy rainfall, the monsoon is expected to slip into a lull phase. It is likely to show brief signs of revival towards the end of the first week of August, coinciding with the formation of a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal. However, the anticipated position and track of the system are not favourable for any substantial increase in rainfall over Kerala. After this, the State is likely to witness a relatively prolonged dry spell, she said.

In addition, the expected peak of El Niño, the periodic warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean that tends to weaken the Indian monsoon, during August and September, coupled with the persistence of neutral Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) conditions, has diminished the prospects of good monsoon rainfall during the remainder of the season. There is a slight possibility that the IOD could turn positive towards the end of September, which could improve monsoon prospects. However, it remains to be seen whether it would be strong enough to minimise the impact of the anticipated strong El Niño, Ms. Gopal said.

During the last El Niño year (2023–24), India, including Kerala, witnessed one of the driest Augusts on record. Kerala received only 86 mm of rainfall against the normal 445.2 mm during the month. The summer that followed also witnessed record-breaking temperatures, with Kerala experiencing a heat wave for the first time in its recorded history.

articles.title: The fiscal cost of cash-transfer schemes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: A social policy is often based on expected electoral gain, and is implemented without any ex ante appraisal; since cash transfers and subsidies are perpetual in nature and politically hard to reverse, such continuous commitment of financial resources demands prior evaluation and real-time monitoring to address potential shortcomings

Business Standard reported on May 13, 2026 that “Cash-transfer promises have moved from the margins of Indian election manifestos to the centre of political competition, with parties across States promising monthly or one-time payments.” Quoting a PRS Legislative Research report, it further said, “12 States are expected to spend nearly ₹1.68 trillion on unconditional cash-transfer schemes for women in 2025-26, … the outgo is roughly equivalent to 0.5 per cent of India’s GDP, compared with less than 0.2 per cent two years ago.”

The RBI report ‘State Finance: Study of State Budgets 2025-26’ reported that the total subsidy outlay increased from ₹1.87 trillion in 2018-19 to ₹4.26 trillion in 2025-26. States often implement promises from their election manifestos soon after forming the government and just before the next election, without any serious assessment of needs or financial commitments.

Conception and funding of an infrastructure project are guided by a Detailed Project Report (DPR) that specifies objectives, alternatives considered, financial and economic analysis, risk mitigation, baseline data, and success criteria. A social policy, by contrast, is often the outcome of an electoral promise or based on expected electoral gain, and is implemented without any comparable ex ante appraisal. Social policies affect human capabilities more directly than infrastructure projects.

The scarcity of public resources and their alternative uses make ex ante appraisal of social sector schemes essential. Moreover, social policies are vulnerable to electoral clientelism, and should therefore adhere to the same principles of public expenditure as infrastructure projects — evidence, accountability, equity, efficiency and fiscal responsibility as infrastructure. The claim that the benefits of social policies are not quantifiable should not stop ex ante appraisal, as methodologies exist to overcome this barrier.

An ex ante appraisal of a social project leaves an audit trail: the legislature, auditors, the media, and citizens can ask whether the project delivered what it promised. Many social schemes are implemented without the assessment of needs, identification of potential beneficiaries, or adequate funding, and a bureaucratic, top-down, target-chasing approach often replaces a democratic, bottom-up planning and implementation process.
This article explores the fiscal and economic fallout of cash transfers and universal subsidies.

If politics decides the desired social ends of such schemes, public finance and administration should decide the programme’s funding priority, the quantum of funding and the implementation process required to achieve those ends.

Prioritising expenditure is the first step in checking the desirability of public expenditure. For example, the Government of Tamil Nadu allocated nearly ₹1,000 crore in 2026-27 to provide scholarships for girls and boys from Government schools to continue higher education. A recent report in a Tamil Magazine ( Ananda Vikatan , November 18, 2026), based on replies it received to RTI applications, found 7,198 vacancies in permanent teaching positions in Government Arts and Science Colleges. If we include teacher vacancies in professional colleges and universities, the number should be nearly 9,000. Filling these vacancies, delayed for over a decade, would cost ₹1,080 crore per annum, rising every year thereafter. With a huge revenue deficit and fiscal deficit, the State budget lacks the revenue cushion to spend an additional ₹1,080 crore per annum. Prioritising is a normative decision: filling vacancies ensures students learn from regular teachers, whereas funding scholarships alone sends them to colleges without regular teachers.

Deciding the quantum of funding and the process of execution requires ex ante evaluation. This should be explicitly oriented toward designing programmes that maximise impact for a given cost, using behavioural models and micro-simulations to predict the effects of hypothetical programmes before implementation.

For instance, a universal subsidy scheme is a trade-off between inclusion and exclusion errors. If it is truly universal, the scheme commits the error of including the undeserving and thus reduces the per-capita benefit to people in need. In a target-oriented scheme, it commits the error of excluding the deserving, but it increases the per-capita benefit to people in need. The choice between the two requires ex ante appraisal of such schemes.

Cash transfers and subsidies are perpetual in nature as they are politically hard to reverse. Therefore, the continuous commitment of scarce financial resources demands not only prior evaluation but also real-time monitoring and evaluation to redesign and right-size schemes.

In practice, fiscal constraints are addressed through post-hoc adjustments, usually by increasing borrowing or cutting even essential public expenditure. Fiscal constraints should, however, prompt more disciplined choices.

articles.title: Hasina has become a ‘thorn’ in Bangladesh-India ties: Minister Humaiun Kobir
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir says New Delhi is beginning to realise the strain the former Prime Minister’s presence in India is causing to bilateral relations

Sheikh Hasina has become a “thorn” in Bangladesh-India relations, with New Delhi beginning to realise the strain her presence in the country is causing to bilateral ties, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said.

Comparing the deposed Prime Minister to an unwelcome guest who suddenly walks into someone’s home, Mr. Kobir said India was in a difficult position as it could neither send her away nor avoid dealing with her presence, news portal bdnews24 reported.
Read more: Sheikh Hasina’s return gambit tests Bangladesh’s political fault lines
“Hasina has become a thorn in Bangladesh-India relations,” he told reporters at the Foreign Ministry on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
“She has become an irritation, and they understand that this is a problem for the relationship,” Mr. Kobir said.
His remarks came a day after India refrained from commenting on Ms. Hasina’s plan to return to Bangladesh on December 16.

External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that her voluntary return should be treated separately from Dhaka’s extradition request, which New Delhi was examining through established legal processes.
Mr. Kobir reiterated that Ms. Hasina could return only under the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh, either in handcuffs or under strict surveillance.

“She is a criminal. There is one policy for criminals and another for ordinary citizens. She falls under the criminal category. She will come only through the extradition treaty. It is not a matter of her returning; she will be handed over,” he said.
Ms. Hasina’s presence in India has emerged as a contentious issue in bilateral ties since her departure from Bangladesh.
She faces serious legal challenges in her home country, including a death sentence handed down in absentia by a special tribunal over the deadly crackdown on protesters during the 2024 uprising.
Ms. Hasina has denied wrongdoing and questioned the legitimacy of the proceedings.

articles.title: MGM Healthcare Malar launches AI-powered MRI facility in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: According to the hospital, the technology can reduce scan time; a brain MRI that conventionally takes about 35 minutes can now be completed in under 14 minutes
MGM Healthcare Malar, Adyar, has launched an AI-powered MRI facility, offering specialised imaging services for neurological, cardiac, musculoskeletal, spinal, and other conditions.
The facility was inaugurated by J. Radhakrishnan, Chairperson of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

The system uses deep learning algorithms to correct motion-related artefacts and improve image quality, potentially reducing the need for repeat scans. It also offers specialised fetal and breast MRI, cardiac MRI, whole-body imaging, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and perfusion imaging.

According to the hospital, the technology can also reduce scan time. A brain MRI that conventionally takes about 35 minutes can now be completed in under 14 minutes. This could benefit patients who find it difficult to remain still for prolonged periods due to pain or discomfort.

Thinesh Ram, senior consultant and head of Imaging and Interventional Radiology, MGM Healthcare Malar, said the system would enable more detailed evaluation of neural pathways and expand the range of diagnostic assessments.

S. Kripanandh, chief operating officer, MGM Healthcare Malar, Adyar, and group chief business officer, said the facility would strengthen the hospital’s diagnostic capabilities and expand access to advanced imaging services in the neighbourhood.

articles.title: Student sent for mental health care after bringing gun to school in Keralam’s Palakkad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police have warned against spreading unverified claims about the gun on social media

The student who brought a gun to Parudur Higher Secondary School, Pallippuram , was sent to the Government Juvenile Home at Vellimadukunnu, Kozhikode, for counselling and mental health care. The Juvenile Justice Board has ordered that he be kept there until December 5.

The student was produced before the board on Wednesday night and was taken to the juvenile home by the police on Thursday. His statement was recorded at the police station on Wednesday in the presence of his parents.

The magistrate directed that the student be given counselling and other mental health support. The possibility of the case and media coverage affecting his mental health was also considered while deciding to send him to the juvenile home.

Meanwhile, the bullet removed from the injured student’s body has been sent to a forensic laboratory for examination. It was collected from a private hospital at Kottakkal, sealed and produced before the court before being sent for testing.
The injured student will remain under observation at the hospital for another day. His surgery was done on Wednesday, and his condition is satisfactory, hospital authorities said.

The case will be divided between the Thrithala and Pattambi police stations. As the house where the gun was kept is at Kodumunda in Muthuthala panchayat, the investigation into the weapon’s possession and storage will be transferred to Pattambi police station. The case related to the firing will remain with Thrithala police station.
Investigators are trying to establish whether the student’s mother knew that the gun was kept at home. According to the student’s statement, the weapon belonged to his paternal grandfather.
However, both his father and grandfather were dead. The police are collecting evidence before deciding on further action against his mother.

The police have also warned against spreading unverified claims about the gun on social media. Reports that it was made in North India, that the bullet was bought in Punjab and that the weapon had been involved in earlier incidents were not confirmed.

Student sent for mental health care after bringing gun to school in Keralam’s Palakkad

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Police have warned against spreading unverified claims about the gun on social media

The student who brought a gun to Parudur Higher Secondary School, Pallippuram , was sent to the Government Juvenile Home at Vellimadukunnu, Kozhikode, for counselling and mental health care. The Juvenile Justice Board has ordered that he be kept there until December 5.

The student was produced before the board on Wednesday night and was taken to the juvenile home by the police on Thursday. His statement was recorded at the police station on Wednesday in the presence of his parents.

The magistrate directed that the student be given counselling and other mental health support. The possibility of the case and media coverage affecting his mental health was also considered while deciding to send him to the juvenile home.

Meanwhile, the bullet removed from the injured student’s body has been sent to a forensic laboratory for examination. It was collected from a private hospital at Kottakkal, sealed and produced before the court before being sent for testing.

The injured student will remain under observation at the hospital for another day. His surgery was done on Wednesday, and his condition is satisfactory, hospital authorities said.

The case will be divided between the Thrithala and Pattambi police stations. As the house where the gun was kept is at Kodumunda in Muthuthala panchayat, the investigation into the weapon’s possession and storage will be transferred to Pattambi police station. The case related to the firing will remain with Thrithala police station.

Investigators are trying to establish whether the student’s mother knew that the gun was kept at home. According to the student’s statement, the weapon belonged to his paternal grandfather.

However, both his father and grandfather were dead. The police are collecting evidence before deciding on further action against his mother.

The police have also warned against spreading unverified claims about the gun on social media. Reports that it was made in North India, that the bullet was bought in Punjab and that the weapon had been involved in earlier incidents were not confirmed.

The incident has also raised questions about security checks at the Parudur Higher Secondary School. articles.title: Alathur MLA withdraws remarks on school shooting in Keralam’s Palakkad, expresses regret
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Admitting that his statement on the incident was factually incorrect, T. M. Sasi expresses unconditional regret over the comment

T.M. Sasi, MLA from Alathur, has withdrawn his remarks that the student who brought a gun to Parudur Higher Secondary School, Pallippuram, had done so with the intention of killing a classmate. Admitting that the statement was factually incorrect, Mr. Sasi expressed unconditional regret over the comment.

Mr. Sasi made the controversial remarks at the valedictory function of the Alathur sub-district school arts festival at SMM Higher Secondary School, Pazhambalacode, on November 25. He had described the shooting as planned and said the student had brought the gun to kill a fellow student.
However, the police said that there was no previous enmity between the students and that the gun went off accidentally when the student brought it from home to show his classmates.

In a statement, Mr. Sasi said his remarks were based on media reports and discussions published on November 24. He admitted that he had failed to take note of subsequent information and should not have made the statement without verifying the facts.

He said he had referred to the incident while expressing concern over violent tendencies among the younger generation. However, he acknowledged that relying on initial reports had led to the incorrect statement.

Mr. Sasi said he had learnt the importance of verifying facts before commenting on such incidents and would exercise greater caution in future as an elected representative. He formally withdrew the remarks and expressed unconditional regret.

articles.title: Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Tamil Nadu Governor seeks CM Vijay’s report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction.

Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam.

The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple — on Tuesday (November 24), defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement.”

Sources told The Hindu that the Governor had sought a report from the Chief Minister under Article 167(b) of the Constitution, detailing the action taken by the authorities on the Supreme Court’s directions.

It came on the heels of the Madurai Collector telling the Supreme Court, in a preliminary status report filed on Wednesday (November 25), that he had made every arrangement to comply with the court’s November 20 order to light the lamp on the deepathoon , but the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniyaswamy Temple had failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team.

articles.title: AP Cabinet clears investment proposals worth ₹36,000 crore, approves Kia’s second plant
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The meeting also approves MSME Right to Business Bill intended to reduce delays in setting up industries and facilitate ease of doing business, major Amaravati infrastructure projects and power sector proposals

The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, on Friday approved investment proposals worth around ₹36,000 crore from six companies, besides clearing a series of policy and infrastructure proposals aimed at accelerating industrial development and creating employment opportunities in the State.

The Cabinet meeting, held at the State Secretariat, lasted nearly three hours and approved 30 agenda items. A key decision was the approval of the Andhra Pradesh MSME Right to Business Bill, 2026, intended to reduce delays in setting up industries and facilitate ease of doing business, sources said.

Among the major investment proposals cleared was Kia’s second automobile manufacturing plant at Penukonda in Sri Sathya Sai district, involving an investment of ₹19,000 crore. The Cabinet also approved Adani’s Integrated Titanium Complex at Srikakulam, with an investment of ₹13,667 crore, and a Saint-Gobain float glass manufacturing facility at Atchutapuram at an outlay of ₹1,800 crore.
The proposals of the six companies had been firmed up during the CII Partnership Summit.

On Amaravati’s development, the Cabinet approved an increase in the estimated cost of the integrated Secretariat and Heads of Departments’ offices from ₹4,688 crore to ₹6,641 crore. It also cleared funds for the construction of the High Court, Assembly and Secretariat buildings.

The Cabinet approved infrastructure works worth ₹1,215 crore for village panchayats in Amaravati and a proposal to construct Amaravati Sangamam at Shakamuru at an estimated cost of ₹626 crore. Development works worth ₹180.68 crore under Green Works Package-2 were also cleared.

In the energy sector, the Cabinet authorised APGENCO to establish a joint venture with Coal India to meet the State’s electricity requirements. It also approved the allocation of 1,127 acres at Myavaram in Kadapa district for a 1,000 MW solar power project and the transfer of a 210 MW wind power project in Nandyal district.
A compressed biogas plant with a capacity of 12 tonnes a day in Prakasam district was also approved.

The Cabinet further cleared the removal of 9,917 acres in Anantapur district from the prohibited properties list and amendments to land records benefiting 4,352 pattadars in the district. Corrections to Webland records pertaining to 10,192 acres in the Railway Koduru area were also approved.
It, however, stipulated that no fresh rights should be created over government, assigned or disputed lands while resolving land-related issues.

articles.title: Film ‘Aalochana’ releases across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The film ‘Aalochana’, featuring veteran actors Narasimha Raju, Prasad Babu, Jayalalitha, Narayana Rao and Maharshi Raghava, was released across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana on Friday, November 27.

Speaking to the media, film director and MA AP founder Dileep Raja said the film aimed to remind children of their responsibility towards parents who had crossed 60 years of age. He said film director Surender Chacha made the movie to inspire young generation in recognising the value of parents.
The story highlights the importance of caring for elderly parents and discourages sending them to old age homes or causing them distress, he said.

Mr. Dileep Raja described the film as a different attempt in Telugu cinema and appealed to people across Andhra Pradesh to support its message. Actor Samudrala Sridhar Sharma and others attended the press conference.

articles.title: Hackers breach U.S. Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so ⁠during work to upgrade the system, two people familiar with the matter said

Hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with ‌the matter told Reuters , in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, ​personnel and logistics data.

The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so ⁠during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen.

In ‌a statement to Reuters , the Air Force said it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the ‌Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities."

Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve ‌as ⁠a one-stop shop for the Air Force's IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft, Amazon, ⁠Oracle and Alphabet — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay or logistics and maintenance.

Among them are the Air Force's Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air defence radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions ​System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than ‌200 U.S. Air Force locations around the world.
SAIC was the prime contractor for Cloud One until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force.
Cloud One is among the U.S. military's biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources.

articles.title: Is stubble burning in Punjab affecting Sri Lanka’s air quality?

fullParagraphs: Pollution from northern India and the wider region travels over the Bay of Bengal to Sri Lanka during the northeast monsoon, and crop burning is part of that mix
In the months of October and November, farmers in Punjab and Haryana burn leftover rice stalks to clear their fields for wheat. The smoke chokes Delhi, but it does not stay there.

articles.title: Arsenic in the water: Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits
As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation.
Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits.

Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group on the issue — also attended by the Chinese Ambassador — where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were causing the pollution downstream. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers.

But there was no public agreement to Thailand's request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar's military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent.
Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead.

Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. "Now with the mines the fish are all gone," she said.
At the joint talks, Thai Ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side.

"Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar's) Shan state, no-one disagrees," Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue.

Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. "This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity," he told AFP . But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be "really difficult", he added.

Multiple ethnic armed groups have been operating there for decades, while a 2021 military coup sparked an ongoing civil war. Thai officials pinpointed two gold mines just over the border from Mae Sai as the main source of high arsenic levels in the Sai River.
Different groups control different parts of the wider area, among them Myanmar military and the United Wa State Army, an ethnic armed group with close ties to China.

Many mining operations in Myanmar are run by Chinese companies, and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul raised pollution with President Xi Jinping this month. "China acknowledged that they are aware of mining by private Chinese companies in Shan state," Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said. "China made clear that they do not support activities that are improper, illegal or cause harm."

articles.title: COP31: India welcomes $50 million climate fund pledge, says adaptation needs far greater
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: India has welcomed a $50 million pledge to the Adaptation Fund at the UN climate change conference COP31 , but said the contribution was inadequate given the scale of adaptation needs in developing countries and stressed that financial pledges must translate into timely and accessible resources.

In a written interview with PTI , Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said the removal of the $120 billion adaptation finance figure from the proposed cover text, and the failure to reach an overarching agreement at COP31, were disappointing.

“The absence of an agreed formulation on the $120 billion adaptation finance figure in the final outcome is disappointing. It reflects the continuing difficulties in securing predictable financial commitments and agreement on how progress towards the existing goal of tripling adaptation finance by 2035 should be measured and monitored,” he said.

Mr. Yadav, however, noted that the absence of a cover decision did not extinguish developed countries’ commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Paris Agreement.

He said adaptation was not a secondary consideration but an immediate developmental necessity for millions of vulnerable people. India had consistently maintained that adaptation finance must be adequate, predictable, primarily public and substantially grant-based, he added.

“Developing countries should not be compelled to incur additional debt to protect vulnerable communities from climate impacts. At COP31, India worked closely with Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) and G77 (largest bloc of 134 developing nations plus China) partners to seek stronger outcomes on adaptation finance and implementation support,” Yadav said.

He said India would continue to push for enhanced financial support, transparency in delivery and implementation of existing commitments, particularly for the poorest and most climate-vulnerable countries.

Mr. Yadav said that the failure to reach consensus on the proposed overarching agreement, the Antalya Pact, should not overshadow progress made on other issues and that the nation continues to deliver substantial climate action through its domestic efforts and resources.

“India engaged constructively throughout the Conference, working closely with BASIC, Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDCs) and G77 to secure a balanced and equitable outcome. We regret that consensus on the proposed Antalya Pact could not be reached. However, this should not overshadow the substantive progress achieved on several important issues,” he said.

On procedural decisions at COP31, Mr. Yadav said the Climate Finance Work Programme decision had established a process for further discussions, while the outcome on the Just Transition Work Programme was more substantive.

The Climate Finance Work Programme decision provides for discussions ahead of COP32 and COP33, including submissions by parties, workshops, virtual dialogues and a high-level ministerial roundtable in 2027.
“While agreement on its substantive scope remains outstanding, the decision provides an opportunity to advance discussions on developed countries’ obligations,” he said.

articles.title: Bombay High Court puts road project on hold till State files report on mangrove loss, compensatory measures
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Bombay High Court directed the State to submit figures documenting tree cover, losses, and five-year survival rates before any orders are passed

The Bombay High Court has withheld permission for a road project in Mumbai until the State government submits a detailed report on measures taken to compensate for the loss of mangroves. The court also stated that ‘afforestation’ efforts must be completed before seeking clearances and that the process should not be treated as a mere formality.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh C. Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna made these remarks while hearing a plea by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) seeking permission to divert 0.2869 hectares of mangrove land in the Bandra-Kurla Complex area to construct an Automated Rapid Transit System covering 8.85 km.

A 2018 High Court ruling mandated court approval for developments affecting wetlands. Though the project will not require clearing mangroves, it impacts six trees, necessitating the planting of 100 trees as compensation.

Advocate Saket Mone, representing the MMRDA, argued that the Automated Rapid Transit System fulfills key connectivity needs. He added that tree planting falls under the jurisdiction of the Forest Department. In response, the Bench questioned why officials had not initiated remedial action when conceptualising the project.

Advocate General of Maharashtra Milind Sathe attributed the planting delays to a shortage of saline land, noting that saplings must be planted before the monsoon to ensure survival. However, the Bench pointed out a gap between regulators’ filings and ground reality, questioning how authorities could grant permission when rules mandate 30% tree cover.

The Court directed the State to submit figures documenting tree cover, losses, and five-year survival rates before any orders are passed. Stating that it does not oppose the project but will not proceed without full compliance, the Court posted the matter to November 30.
Mr. Mone was briefed by advocate Fatema Ansari, while Mr. Sathe was briefed by Government Pleader Onkar Chandurkar.

articles.title: 68-year-old man gets 20-year RI in POCSO case in Palnadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Guntur special court sentenced a 68-year-old man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment in a POCSO case.

In a press release here on Friday, Palnadu district Superintendent of Police Jagadeesh Adahalli informed that the accused, Bojja Nageswara Rao, son of Venkateswarlu, of Uday Nagar Colony near Sivapuram Thanda in Nekarikallu mandal of Palnadu district, was convicted by the Special Court for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO), Guntur.

Special Judge Shami Parvin Sultana Begum awarded him 20 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of ₹1,000 under Section 6 read with Sections 5(l) and 5(m) of the POCSO Act. He was also sentenced to five years of simple imprisonment and a fine of ₹1,000 under Section 10 of the Act, besides six months of simple imprisonment under Section 506 of the IPC.
The court ordered that all sentences run concurrently and directed that the fine amount be utilised for the victim’s welfare and rehabilitation.
Considering the accused’s submission regarding his health condition, the court directed prison authorities to provide him with necessary medical treatment, medicines and appropriate food.

The Superintendent of Police said stringent legal action would be taken against those committing sexual offences against children. He lauded Sattenapalli Rural Circle Inspector Kiran, Nekarikallu Sub Inspector Satish and the Court Monitoring Cell personnel for expediting the investigation and ensuring conviction.

articles.title: Wayanad declared India’s first e-waste-free district
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 102.8 tonnes of discarded electronic waste collected during a two-month drive in four phases across the district; Suchitwa Mission issues protocol to sustain the initiative, while a separate action plan is launched to make tourist destinations plastic-free
Wayanad, nestled in the Western Ghats, has officially been declared India’s first e-waste-free model district.

The declaration follows a massive two-month collection drive led by the Suchitwa Mission in association with Haritha Karma Sena (HKS) volunteers, local self-government institutions and accredited recycling agencies. During the campaign, teams collected 102.8 tonnes of discarded electronic items, ranging from old computers and mobile phones to household appliances, from homes, educational institutions, offices and commercial establishments across the district.

Making the declaration at a function in Kalpetta on Friday (November 27, 2026), Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan said the achievement, realised through collective effort and dedication, was invaluable and served as a model not only for Keralam but also for the entire country.

“By declaring itself e-waste-free, Wayanad sends a powerful message to other districts that such a feat is indeed possible. This mission instils great confidence that the entire State can be made completely free of e-waste. Through this collective endeavour, Wayanad has successfully addressed a menace that poses a threat to health and the natural environment,” said Mr. Satheesan.

The drive was carried out in four phases. In the first phase, electronic waste was collected and removed from all government institutions across the district. In the second phase, collection points were established at various locations in all local self-government institutions, including 23 grama panchayats and three municipalities. In the third phase, HKS members visited every household in the district to collect e-waste. In the fourth phase, special collection points were set up at each local self-government institution to collect e-waste from those who had been unable to participate in the earlier stages. The collected waste was handed over to the Clean Kerala Company for scientific processing.
To ensure the sustainability of the initiative, the Suchitwa Mission has issued a protocol outlining the measures to be adopted by local self-government institutions and government offices.

Meanwhile, a major initiative to make tourist destinations in the hill district completely plastic-free was also launched at the function. According to officials, once the system is in place, strict restrictions will be imposed on bringing plastic products to tourist destinations and using them there. Agriculture Minister T. Siddique released the e-waste-free district protocol and the plastic-free destination action plan.

articles.title: Telangana to provide financial assistance to 7,000 unemployed youth from EWS seeking jobs abroad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana government has introduced the Chief Minister’s Overseas Employment Scheme to provide financial assistance to unemployed youth from economically weaker families seeking jobs abroad.
The scheme, to be implemented through the Telangana Overseas Manpower Company Limited (TOMCOM), envisages extending benefits to 7,000 candidates during the 2026–27 financial year.

The government issued guidelines for the scheme through G.O. No. 19, providing for a 50% subsidy on expenditure incurred towards foreign language training, visa processing and air travel, subject to specified ceilings.
Of the 7,000 proposed beneficiaries, 5,880 will be candidates seeking direct overseas employment, while 1,120 will be those applying for jobs that require proficiency in foreign languages.

Under the first category, candidates who can take up overseas jobs without specialised foreign language training or examinations will be eligible for a subsidy towards visa and air travel expenses. The government will consider expenditure of up to ₹1 lakh and provide 50% assistance, subject to a maximum of ₹50,000.

The second category covers candidates seeking jobs that require proficiency in the language of the destination country. Expenditure of up to ₹3.5 lakh will be considered, with the government providing 50% subsidy subject to a ceiling of ₹1.75 lakh. The remaining 50% of the expenditure will have to be borne by beneficiaries.

Candidates aged between 18 and 40 years will be eligible. Applicants must be Telangana natives and should have studied from Class VI to X in the State. Only one member of a family, as identified through the ration card, will be eligible for the subsidy. At least 33.33% of the benefits will be reserved for women and 5% for persons with disabilities.
Applications will be received exclusively through a dedicated online portal to be launched shortly by TOMCOM.

articles.title: Hyderabad’s elevated roads are ‘poisonous rivers’, says former Bogotá mayor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Former Bogota mayor Enrique Peñalosa has criticised Hyderabad’s reliance on elevated roads and high-speed corridors, describing them as “poisonous rivers” that divide neighbourhoods, restrict pedestrian movement and affect the value of properties around them.

Speaking during a discussion on public transport at Cyberabad Moves on Friday, Peñalosa said urban roads should be designed around people and public spaces rather than prioritising the movement of private vehicles. He argued that high-speed roads without traffic signals made it difficult for pedestrians and cyclists to cross, while elevated roads created barriers between communities.
“Human beings cannot work next to a high-velocity road. They cannot go by bicycle. They cannot go across,” he said, arguing that such infrastructure often treated pedestrians as an afterthought.

Peñalosa said high-speed roads also affected the value of land and properties in their vicinity because of noise and the difficulty of accessing areas on either side. He questioned whether people would want to live next to such roads and said cities should consider the wider impact of transport infrastructure on their surroundings.

He cited the Champs-Élysées in Paris as an example of how a major avenue could accommodate heavy traffic without sacrificing its character as a public space. The avenue has multiple traffic lanes, but also wide footpaths, trees, shops, traffic signals and bus services.
The former mayor said that such streets are attractive due to the environment they offered pedestrians and visitors, rather than simply the number of vehicles they could carry.

He also questioned the argument that Hyderabad needed wider roads to address congestion. Increasing road width would not necessarily improve mobility if the additional space was used to accommodate more private vehicles, he said. Instead, cities needed to make deliberate choices about allocating road space to buses, pedestrians and cyclists.

Peñalosa welcomed the proposal for a dedicated contra-flow bus corridor, saying it was encouraging to see Hyderabad consider exclusive lanes for buses. He said public transport should be given priority on existing roads rather than designing new arrangements that avoided affecting private vehicle movement.

The discussion also touched on the need to plan urban growth around public transport. Peñalosa said density was essential for high-frequency and affordable public transport, but stressed that density had to be accompanied by footpaths, parks and public spaces.
The session brought together representatives of TGSRTC, HUMTA, South Central Railway and WRI India to discuss public transport, road planning and the city’s mobility challenges.

articles.title: Allahabad High Court scraps UPPSC PCS 2025 prelims result over reservation rules, orders fresh mains
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court said that the unreserved category was open to all candidates and could not be treated as a category reserved for those who had not claimed reservation

The Allahabad High Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) cancelled the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission’s (UPPSC) preliminary examination results of the Provincial Civil Services (PCS) 2025, holding that the commission had wrongly excluded meritorious reserved-category candidates from the unreserved category while preparing the category-wise merit lists.
A Bench of Justice Manish Kumar Nigam directed the commission to redraw the preliminary merit list and conduct the mains examination afresh on the basis of the revised results.

The ruling came on a petition filed by Sanjay Kumar and three other candidates belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). The petitioners contended that the UPPSC had failed to consider reserved-category candidates who scored more than the last selected unreserved-category candidate for the open-category list.

In a supplementary affidavit before the court, the commission disclosed that 2,993 OBC, 464 Scheduled Caste (SC), 155 Scheduled Tribe (ST), and 921 EWS candidates had scored more than the last selected unreserved-category candidate in the preliminary examination. The combined figure stood at 4,533.
The commission also disclosed that, after the mains examination, 579 OBC, 158 SC, five ST, and 168 EWS candidates had scored above the last selected unreserved-category candidate.

The petitioners argued that candidates securing marks above the unreserved-category cut-off should be considered against open-category vacancies, irrespective of their social category. They contended that restricting such candidates to their respective reserved categories violated the constitutional guarantees of equality and equal opportunity in public employment under Articles 14 and 16. They also relied on Section 3(6) of the Uttar Pradesh Public Services (Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes) Act, 1994.

Rejecting the commission’s approach, the court observed that the unreserved category was open to all candidates and could not be treated as a category reserved for those who had not claimed reservation.

“The respondents have wrongly applied the law... in preparing the list category-wise, both at the stage of Preliminary Examination as well as mains examination, treating unreserved category to be a category reserved for candidates, who have not claimed any reservation,” the court said.

The court also quashed Condition 19 of the PCS-2025 advertisement, which provided for the adjustment of reserved-category candidates against unreserved vacancies only at the final selection stage, subject to their not having availed any relaxation in the qualifying standard. It held that the condition had no legal basis after the commission’s office memorandum dated January 9, 2020, on the issue had already been quashed in a connected case.

Consequently, the court set aside the preliminary examination result declared on December 1, 2025, and directed the UPPSC to redraw the merit list for the advertised vacancies and hold the mains examination afresh on the basis of the revised result. The commission will thereafter proceed with the remaining stages of the selection process.

articles.title: ECI announces revised schedule for Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under the revised schedule, the draft roll will be published on December 15, claims and objections can be filed from December 15 to January 14, and the final roll will be published on February 8
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday (November 27, 2026) released a revised schedule for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal.

Under the revised schedule, the qualifying date remains January 1, 2027. Polling stations will be rationalised by December 3, the draft roll will be published on December 15, claims and objections can be filed from December 15 to January 14, and the final roll will be published on February 8.
In the earlier schedule, draft electoral rolls were to be published on November 23, and the final voters’ list on January 16, 2027.
The ECI also issued a slew of clarifications regarding electors still marked ‘Under Adjudication’ during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

According to the letter sent to the Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal, for cases still marked ‘Under Adjudication, if a Judicial Officer has passed an order but has not e-signed it, the case will be treated as decided. The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) will update the roll according to the written decision. However, cases not yet adjudicated will go to the EROs for appropriate decisions.
No action will be taken for electors whose names have been deleted but who have not appealed as they stand excluded by the Judicial Officers’ orders.

For deleted electors whose appeals are pending, the Supreme Court’s directions of November 23 on prioritising appeals must be followed. “If these persons file Form 6 for fresh inclusion, EROs should not process it until the Appellate Tribunal decides the appeal,” the ECI letter said.
For appeals decided in favour of exclusion, the tribunal’s decision should be implemented.

The ECI also revised the honorarium paid to the judges of the Appellate Tribunal. While a former Chief Justice of a High Court will now get ₹2,60,000, former judges of a High Court will get ₹2,50,000 per month.
More than 37 lakh cases are stuck in the 19 appellate tribunals.

articles.title: RBI cuts daily CRR maintenance to 90%, to unlock over ₹40,000 crore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The latest relaxation is expected to improve banks’ liquidity flexibility and support credit deployment.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday eased the minimum daily maintenance requirement for the cash reserve ratio (CRR) from 99% to 90%, a move expected to release more than ₹40,000 crore into the banking system and provide banks with additional funds for lending.

“On the basis of an assessment of the current and evolving macroeconomic situation and liquidity conditions, it has been decided to reduce the minimum daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) from 99% of the requirement to 90% effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026,” the RBI said.

Under the revised arrangement, scheduled banks will be required to maintain at least 90% of their prescribed CRR on each day of the reporting fortnight. However, the average daily CRR maintained during the fortnight must not fall below the level prescribed by the RBI.

With the prescribed CRR currently at 3% of a bank’s net demand and time liabilities (NDTL), banks will now have greater flexibility in managing their daily cash balances, while continuing to meet the overall fortnightly requirement.

The latest move reverses the tightening introduced on October 9, shortly after the previous Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting. At the time, the RBI had raised the minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement from 90% to 99%, effective from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026.
The earlier move came when the banking system was flush with liquidity following substantial mobilisation of funds through foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits.

articles.title: Hyderabad’s air pollution puts focus on hospitals; doctors call for city-level health database
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Hospitals want to share anonymised data on respiratory illnesses, strokes and cardiovascular conditions, while doctors propose using daily AQI readings to alert vulnerable patients

With Hyderabad recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of over 300 on Deepavali and many other days recording poor air quality earlier this year, doctors and public health experts have called for a coordinated effort by hospitals to track the health effects of pollution and build a city-level database that can help shape public policy.

The issue came into focus during a panel discussion on ‘Impact of Mobility on Air Quality and Public Health’ at Cyberabad Moves, where doctors said that the effects of polluted air went beyond respiratory illnesses and were also linked to cardiovascular problems and strokes. They stressed that the health consequences of daily exposure to pollution, particularly during commutes, needed to be documented through local medical data.

Pawan Mukulutla of WRI India, who moderated the discussion, pointed out that congestion was only the most visible consequence of the way people travelled. The less visible costs included exposure to polluted air, unsafe roads and the lack of pedestrian infrastructure. He cited Hyderabad’s AQI crossing 300 on Deepavali and said particulate matter levels, including PM2.5 and PM10, had been several times above prescribed thresholds.

Dr. Sudheer Vinnamala, Regional Medical Director of KIMS, said hospitals could work together to create a Hyderabad-level health database by sharing anonymised information on respiratory illnesses, strokes and cardiovascular conditions with public health authorities.

“What you can’t measure, you can’t manage,” he said, arguing that such a database could help identify vulnerable groups and establish a clearer picture of the relationship between air quality and health outcomes.

He said doctors could also use daily AQI information to alert patients with asthma and other respiratory conditions when pollution levels deteriorated, allowing them to take precautions and avoid unnecessary exposure. Hospitals could play a role in reducing pollution and traffic by encouraging carpooling, staggering appointments and arranging last-mile transport links from Metro stations.

Dr Vishwanath Gella, a pulmonologist at AIG Hospitals, said pollution affected people with and without pre-existing health conditions. He said doctors were seeing patients with asthma, respiratory infections and other lung-related complaints, with an increase in cases during periods of poor air quality, particularly around Deepavali and in winter.

Dr Shailaja Tetali of the Public Health Foundation of India said research into school travel patterns showed that around 80 per cent of children lived within two to three kilometres of their schools. A majority travelled by public transport, walked or cycled.

While walking and cycling offered physical activity, children using these modes were also exposed to roadside pollution and faced road safety risks. She said improving infrastructure around schools could address several of these concerns, as interventions within a three-kilometre radius could cover a large proportion of children’s daily journeys.

She called for authorities to act on existing evidence instead of repeatedly commissioning studies, suggesting that interventions could first be tested in smaller areas and then replicated across the city.

Orthopaedic surgeon Dr Gurava Reddy of KIMS-Sunshine Hospitals said poorly designed roads and junctions contributed to crashes, pointing to inadequate visibility, obstructed sightlines and sudden turning movements as factors that made roads dangerous.
He said several improvements could be made through better road engineering without requiring large investments, provided authorities were willing to address design flaws.

articles.title: Robotic technology can improve precision and recovery in knee replacement, say experts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The webinar discussed the role of robotics in improving surgical precision, implant positioning and recovery in total knee replacement

The Hindu , in association with Kauvery Hospital, conducted a webinar on Friday titled ‘The Role of Robotics in Knee Replacement’. Orthopaedic specialists discussed the use of robotic-assisted technology in total knee replacement (TKR), its benefits, post-operative recovery, costs and the role of surgeons in performing the procedure.

The experts were Mukunth K., senior consultant, orthopaedic surgeon, joint replacement and sports injuries, Kauvery Hospital, Alwarpet; P.R. Ramasamy, head of the department of orthopaedics and pelviacetabular and joint replacement surgeon, Kauvery Hospital, Tiruchi; and Manivannan, consultant, orthopaedics, arthroscopy and joint replacement surgeon, Kauvery Hospital, Salem.

Dr. Mukunth explained how robotic-assisted technology helps surgeons plan knee replacement procedures through bone mapping, precise measurements and real-time guidance. He said the technology helped surgeons make accurate bone cuts and position implants closer to the intended alignment. He compared the robot’s role to GPS navigation, emphasising that the surgeon remained in control of the procedure.

He said manual measurements during conventional surgery could vary by 2–3 mm, even in experienced hands. Greater precision in bone cuts and implant alignment could help reduce soft-tissue trauma and blood loss during surgery and improve post-operative outcomes.

Dr. Ramasamy explained the steps involved in robotic-assisted knee replacement. He said the procedure involved less damage to the surrounding bone, which could make a future revision surgery easier. He also clarified that robotic technology was not used for revision surgery in patients who had undergone conventional knee replacement 15–20 years earlier. The aim of robotic-assisted TKR was not limited to pain relief but also included helping patients return to their routine activities sooner, he said.

Dr. Manivannan discussed post-operative recovery and mobility. articles.title: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri appointed as J&K’s Advocate General after two year gap
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Faisal is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice; the Omar Abdullah government in April had proposed the names for the post while the appointment came after the J&K High Court heard a PIL plea on November 5 regarding the vacant post

Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was on Friday (November 27, 2026) appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir, eight months after the territorial government forwarded the proposal to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for his approval. The J&K government has been without an Advocate General for more than two years.

“In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 79 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (Act No. 34 of 2019) and in supersession of notification S.O. No. 07 of 2019 dated 01-11-2019, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is pleased to appoint Mr. Syed Faisal Qadri, Senior Advocate, as Advocate General for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir,” reads the official order.

Mr. Qadri is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice. With over 100 reported judgments, Mr. Faisal earned a name for himself by pleading cases of both private and government institutions in the J&K High Court and in the Supreme Court.

The Omar Abdullah government in April this year had proposed the names for the post. The appointment, however, came after the J&K High Court heard a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on November 5 regarding the vacant post. Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli had apprised the Division Bench, comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajnesh Oswal, that the appointment would be made within a period of one month.

It is a major relief for Chief Minister Omar Abdullah whose government was pursuing many pending policy matters before the J&K High Court in the past two years. Mr. Abdullah’s party National Conference (NC) had won the Assembly elections in 2024, but remained without an Advocate General since then.
In 2019, senior advocate D.C. Raina was appointed as the Advocate General of J&K. He, later, tendered his resignation in October 2024.

articles.title: Modi invokes Lord Murugan; BJP says Tamil Nadu Government acted against Hindus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Supreme Court has exposed Tamil Nadu Government’s anti-Sanatan mindset, says Nitin Nabin

Hours after the Supreme Court directed that the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam be lit at the deepathoon (stone pillar) on the Thirupparankundram hill on November 28, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday posted a message on X invoking Lord Murugan.
“Vetrivel Muruganukku Arogara [Victory to Lord Murugan, bearer of the sacred spear!],” said Mr. Modi. The same message was posted in Tamil and Hindi too.
Earlier, t he BJP welcomed the Supreme Court’s directive, describing it as a major victory for devotees of Lord Murugan and accusing the Tamil Nadu Government of acting against the Hindu community.

While hearing contempt petitions over the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the deepathoon , the Supreme Court observed that the chain of events indicate that the Executive authorities had acted “according to the dictates of their political bosses”.
Despite a Supreme Court directive, the ceremonial lamp was lit at the traditional location on November 24, and not at the deepathoon, located near a dargah.

Through a post on X , BJP president Nitin Nabin said the top court’s order was a historic victory for every devotee of Lord Murugan. “By ordering the ceremonial lamp to be lit at the Thiruparankundram deepathoon tomorrow [November 28] and pulling up Tamil Nadu authorities for acting at the dictates of their political bosses, the Hon’ble Supreme Court has thoroughly exposed the INDI Alliance government’s anti-Sanatan mindset,” he said. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, is a part of the INDIA bloc.

“No political conspiracy can stop the sacred traditions of Bharat. May the divine blessings of Lord Murugan protect all devotees and guide them on the path of courage and righteousness. Vetri Vel! Veera Vel!,” Mr. Nabin said.

At a press conference, BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister of hating “Sanatan traditions and the Hindu community”. “This hatred is so deep that a Chief Minister who has taken oath under the Constitution of India to protect and preserve the ethos of the Constitution wilfully decided to violate it,” he alleged.

Alleging that the INDIA alliance and Mr. Vijay were “hell-bent on violating the orders of the Supreme Court and hurting the sentiments of the Hindu community”, Mr. Bhatia said the “tolerant” Hindu community took the legal route and approached the top court.

“It is a rap on their knuckles by the Hon’ble Supreme Court...When I say that the Constitution of India is the life and soul of our democracy, questions will be asked of leaders like Rahul Gandhi and C. Joseph Vijay. When you take an oath under this Constitution, how is it that you can even dare to violate the spirit and the provisions of this Constitution with impunity?” he said.

articles.title: Supreme Court refuses to mandate unified portal for tracing unclaimed deposits; cites regulatory reforms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sucheta Dalal’s petition highlighted the accumulation of unclaimed deposits and investments with financial institutions and the procedural difficulties faced by nominees and legal heirs in recovering them

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) observed that regulatory reforms had substantially addressed the principal concerns raised in a plea seeking to facilitate the identification and recovery of unclaimed bank deposits, mutual fund investments and securities by legal heirs of deceased persons. The court, however, declined to mandate the creation of a unified portal for tracing and reclaiming such assets, noting that substantial sector-specific mechanisms were already in place.

A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and R. Mahadevan disposed of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed in 2022 by journalist and managing editor of Moneylife magazine Sucheta Dalal. The PIL highlighted the accumulation of unclaimed deposits and investments with financial institutions and the procedural difficulties faced by nominees and legal heirs in recovering them.

“…we find that the principal concerns which prompted the institution of the present writ petition have been substantially addressed. The subsequent establishment of centralised search facilities, simplification of claim procedures, strengthening of nomination and transmission mechanisms, and implementation of public awareness initiatives constitute significant progress towards addressing these concerns,” the Bench said, adding that any specific grievance concerning unclaimed financial assets may be pursued before the competent authority in accordance with law.

The petition sought directions to streamline the settlement of claims by legal heirs regarding bank deposits, insurance proceeds, post-office deposits and other financial assets to avoid unnecessary litigation. It also stressed the need for a centralised online database under the aegis of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), providing particulars of deceased account holders, including their names, addresses and the dates of their last transactions.

The Bench noted that the RBI had launched the Unclaimed Deposits, Gateway to Access Information (UDGAM) portal in August 2023, enabling individuals to trace unclaimed deposits across multiple banks through a common platform. The search facility was subsequently extended to 30 banks, which together accounted for approximately 90% of the unclaimed deposits held in the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund (DEAF) in terms of value.

The Department of Financial Services informed the court that unclaimed financial assets worth approximately ₹6,453 crore had been returned to their rightful claimants as of April 18, 2026, through a nationwide campaign titled ‘Aapki Poonji, Aapka Adhikar’, launched in October last year. Outreach and facilitation camps had been organised across 748 districts.

The Bench also noted that the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, permitted bank customers to designate up to four nominees. Revised guidelines issued by the RBI in November last year provided for settling death claims within 15 days of receiving complete documentation, simplified procedures for certain claims involving accounts without nomination of up to ₹15 lakh, and compensation for delays.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for Ms. Dalal, contended that despite these measures, a comprehensive platform still did not exist through which individuals or legal heirs could identify and reclaim financial assets held across different financial institutions. He further submitted that grievances concerning unclaimed insurance proceeds, post-office deposits and provident funds had not been adequately addressed.

The Bench, however, declined to issue such a direction, pointing out that banking, securities, insurance and other financial sectors operated under distinct statutory and regulatory frameworks, with differing requirements concerning ownership, verification and transmission of assets.

“While greater coordination between these mechanisms may be desirable, the establishment of a unified platform involves questions of regulatory policy, technical feasibility and administrative coordination. In the absence of any demonstrated violation requiring judicial intervention, we do not consider it necessary or appropriate to mandate the adoption of one particular institutional arrangement, particularly when substantial sector-specific mechanisms have already been established,” the Bench said.

The court also declined to order a general investigation into unclaimed deposits purportedly belonging to government bodies, welfare schemes and charitable institutions, observing that the mere existence of such deposits did not establish any illegality in their transfer to the DEAF or a failure of regulatory oversight.

Similarly, it refused to issue omnibus directions for penalising banks over alleged non-compliance with RBI circulars in the absence of specific findings of regulatory violations. It clarified that the RBI was at liberty to examine individual instances of default and take appropriate action in accordance with law.
