articles.title: Indian pharma company Hetero begins supply of generic twice-yearly HIV prevention injection in Africa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir as an additional HIV prevention option, based on clinical evidence showing high efficacy in preventing HIV infection

Hyderabad-based pharmaceutical company Hetero has begun phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir, a long-acting drug for HIV prevention, to three African countries. The company plans to supply 300,000 vials initially to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe.
Lenacapavir is used as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Unlike daily oral PrEP medicines, the injectable formulation is administered once every six months.

Hetero is launching the generic drug under the brand names Lexapir and Capvic. The company expects to introduce its generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027. These tablets form part of the PrEP regimen and will be supplied by the original manufacturer, Gilead Sciences, in the interim.

The launch follows Gilead’s non-exclusive voluntary licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers, allowing them to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 eligible countries. The licensing arrangement is intended to expand access to the drug in low- and middle-income countries.

Hetero said its generic injectable formulation and oral initiation tablets had received an Expert Review Panel recommendation, allowing eligible procurement through applicable Global Fund channels while regulatory approval or WHO prequalification processes continue. In Zimbabwe, procurement is being supported through the United Nations Development Programme using Global Fund financing.

The company plans to supply the drug to 10 additional African countries in early 2027 and expand availability across other countries covered by its licence, subject to national regulatory approvals and procurement arrangements. It also plans to introduce generic lenacapavir in India in the coming months, subject to regulatory clearance.

articles.title: BITS Pilani-Hyderabad researchers develop affordable way to grow microalgae
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Researchers at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, have secured an Indian patent for a low-cost nutrient medium that could make large-scale cultivation of microalgae more affordable, opening possibilities for applications in renewable fuels, carbon capture and biotechnology.

The patented innovation, titled “Nutrient Medium Composition for Mass Cultivation of Microalgae” (Patent No. 603126), has been developed by Sandip S. Deshmukh of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, K. Pranav Narayan of the Department of Biological Sciences and research scholar Sama Sanghamitra, as per a press release issued on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

Microalgae are microscopic organisms that use sunlight and carbon dioxide to produce biomass. They are considered a promising resource for wastewater treatment, carbon dioxide capture, biofertilisers, food and nutraceutical products, and the production of biodiesel and other bio-based fuels. However, the high cost of cultivation has limited their large-scale adoption.

The BITS team developed an alternative nutrient formulation using locally available agricultural-grade fertilisers instead of expensive laboratory-grade chemicals. The formulation supplies key nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur required for microalgal growth while reducing the complexity and cost of preparing the cultivation medium.

The macronutrients needed to prepare 100 litres of the new medium cost about ₹2.40, compared with around ₹43 for the conventional Bold’s Basal Medium (BBM). The cost is estimated to be around ₹4.50 per 100 litres, making it significantly cheaper than conventional alternatives.

The formulation is also easy to prepare and can be supplied as a dry powder, which can be dissolved in water before use. The technology was tested in laboratory, non-sterile and outdoor cultivation conditions. The microalgae was also successfully cultivated in a 10,000-litre open pond using natural sunlight and atmospheric carbon dioxide.

Researchers are now in discussions with a potential industry partner, which has proposed a two-month evaluation of the formulation for carbon capture and biomass production applications. They are also seeking collaborations with companies in biofuel, algal biotechnology and carbon management sectors to explore commercialisation of the technology.

articles.title: Mahadevappa turns up for Constitution Day function at Maharaja’s College grounds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Putting to rest speculation about a rift with former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, former Minister H.C. Mahadevappa attended the Constitution Day celebrations organised by the State government at Maharaja’s College grounds in Mysuru on Thursday.
On the eve of the celebrations, Yathindra Siddaramaiah, accompanied by Housing Minister Zameer Ahmed Khan and MLC Naseer Ahmed, visited Mr. Mahadevappa at his residence in Mysuru.

Later in the evening, Mr. Mahadevappa visited Mr. Siddaramaiah’s residence in Kuvempunagar. Speaking to reporters after Mr. Siddaramaiah saw him off, Mr. Mahadevappa denied having any differences with the former Chief Minister. “Once a friend is always a friend,” he remarked, recalling his 40-year-long friendship with Mr. Siddaramaiah.

Mr. Mahadevappa not only attended the Constitution Day celebrations at Maharaja’s College grounds, but also accompanied Mr. Siddaramaiah earlier in the day to garland the statue of B.R. Ambedkar at Town Hall. Both Mr. Siddaramaiah and Mr. Mahadevappa were also present at the Constitution Day programme organised by Dalit organisations at Karnataka State Open University (KSOU) later in the evening.

Mr. Mahadevappa, once considered a close confidant of Mr. Siddaramaiah, was perceived to have distanced himself from the former Chief Minister after being left out of the Cabinet headed by D.K. Shivakumar.

Although Mr. Mahadevappa had taken the initiative to plan the Constitution Day celebrations, announcing a two-day programme as early as the second week of October, the T. Narasipur MLA was conspicuous by his absence at the preparatory meetings convened by Mr. Siddaramaiah in Bengaluru and Mr. Yathindra Siddaramaiah, Minister in-charge of Mysuru district, in Mysuru, sparking rumours of a chill in their relationship.

articles.title: SBI donates ₹4.43 lakh cheque to improve facilities in tribal schools in Parvatipuram -Manyam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), State Bank of India general manager Praful Kumar Jena handed over ₹4.43 lakh cheque to Parvatipuram Joint Collector and Integrated Tribal Development Agency Project Officer R. Viashali towards improving infrastructure and other facilities in tribal welfare schools in Parvatipuram-Manyam district.

In a press release on Thursday, Mr. Jena said that the SBI selected Parvatipuram-Manyam district for CSR activity in recognition of its top performance in the entire State with regard to Class X examinations.
He appreciated Collector N. Prabhakar Reddy for extending support to the banking sector and for the effective implementation of welfare schemes through various bank branches of the district.

Ms. Vaishali thanked the SBI and said that CSR activities of all companies was the need of the hour to improve facilities in educational institutions. SBI officials and Parvatipuram District Educational Officer Brahmaji handed over 30 bicycles to students of a government high school in Parvatipuram.

articles.title: Sporadic incidents of violence mark polling in 23 ULBs and 3,240 Gram Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Polling percentage in ULBs is tentatively put at 62.50, while the Gram Panchayats registered a percentage of 74.67; tension gripped Ahobilam in Nandyal district when the YSRCP supporters resorted to stone-pelting resulting in damage to a few vehicles and injuries to several persons

Elections to the 23 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), including four Municipal Corporations (Kakinada, Mangalagiri - Tadepalli, Rajamahendravaram and Srikakulam), 19 Municipalities / Nagar Panchayats, and 3,240 Gram Panchayats (GPs) ended on Thursday with sporadic incidents of violence reported mostly from the Rayalaseema region.
At 5 p.m., the ULBs registered a polling percentage of 62.50 (tentative), according to the State Election Commission, which pegged the percentage in the GPs at 1 p.m. (close of polling) at 74.67.
The polling began on a peaceful note, but as the day progressed, cadres of the NDA and YSRCP indulged in clashes over alleged irregularities in the conduct of elections.

Amadalavalasa, Rajam, Palacole, Gudur, Bhimavaram, Tadepalligudem, Tanuku, Gudivada, Chinthalapudi, Tadigadapa, Ponnur, Narasaraopeta, Bapatla, Kandukur, Podili, Kavali, Alluru, Srikalahasti and B. Kothakota were the Municipalities and NPs that went to the polls.

TDP and YSRCP workers resorted to mutual accusations, which resulted in tension in Allagadda Mandal of Nandyal district, where the ruling party leaders alleged that YSRCP workers rigged the election, and vice-versa. The TDP leaders said the YSRCP workers threw acid at some of them as their attempts were thwarted.

Elections in Anantapur Rural Mandal were marred by heated arguments between the leaders of TDP and YSRCP over allegations of bogus voting. The police managed to control the situation by dispersing the crowds.
Voters at a polling station in Tanguturu during the first phase of the Gram Panchayat elections in Prakasam district on Thursday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS

In Rajamahendravaram, BJP MLC Somu Veerraju indulged in a war of words with the YSRCP supporters who objected to his presence at a polling station in Ward 62. Tension prevailed for a while at Pavuluru village of Inkollu Mandal in Bapatla district as YSRCP leaders alleged that TDP cadres attacked them in collusion with the police, to rig the election. YSRCP’s Chevireddy Bhaskar Reddy accused officials of favouring the ruling alliance in Chandragiri (Tirupati district) to have its candidates elected unopposed.

Tension gripped Ahobilam in Nandyal district when the YSRCP supporters allegedly resorted to stone- pelting upon Allagadda MLA Bhuma Akhila Priya’s arrival, resulting in damage to some vehicles and injuries to several persons.

Tirupati MP Maddila Gurumoorthy fumed at the TDP leaders for allegedly getting the police to detain YSRCP workers in Srikalahasti and stopping their polling agents from doing their work. Unruly scenes were witnessed at some polling stations in Annamayya and Sri Sathya Sai districts, but the police quickly quelled the mobs.

articles.title: Kannada organisations oppose merger of rural schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A central committee of Kannada organisations to hold various meetings to decide the future course of protest
Kannada organisations in Belagavi have opposed the closure of some rural schools under the Karnataka Public Schools magnet model.
The central committee of Kannada organisations will hold various meetings to decide the future course of protest. This decision was taken at a Rajyotsava event organised in Belagavi on Tuesday.

“The State government is closing down rural schools in the name of merger of schools under the magnet school model. The State government has not cancelled the scheme, despite repeated protests by student organisations,” convenor of the central committee Ashok Chandargi told The Hindu .

“We are seriously concerned about the closure of thousands of Kannada-medium schools under the magnet school scheme. It has now become imperative to launch an intense struggle against these actions,” Mr. Chandargi, who is a member of the Karnataka Border Development Authority, said.

“We have also appealed to all Kannada organizations to take a serious view of the State government’s move to hand over government schools to private entities under the adoption scheme. This is not acceptable,” he said.
“Public safety and law and order, education, healthcare and job creation are the primary responsibilities of any government. No government can wash its hands off its responsibilities,” he said.
“The ruling government must consistently formulate initiatives to protect land, water and language of the State and to ensure the upliftment of the lives of the Kannada people,” he said.

articles.title: Delhi tops list of most polluted NCR cities for PM2.5, PM10 despite no severe AQI days
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days

Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year.

According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69.
For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre.
Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each.

In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025.

A comparison of the same period over the last six years, from 2021 to 2026, shows that Delhi topped the PM2.5 list three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026, while it recorded the highest average PM10 concentration twice, in 2024 and 2026.

Despite topping both pollution charts, Delhi did not record a single day in the severe air quality category during the 56 days. It recorded three days in the satisfactory category, 23 in moderate, 18 in poor and 12 in very poor.

"Air across the NCR has been clearly better this season, helped by good October rain and less pollution reaching Delhi from spread-out and fewer farm fires. The next step is to cut year-round sources such as vehicles, dust and waste burning across the whole region, so this improvement becomes the new normal," Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalyst, told PTI.
The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days.

In 2025, Delhi recorded four satisfactory days, nine moderate days, 13 poor days, 27 very poor days and three severe days. The previous year, air quality remained in the moderate category for 13 days, poor for 10 days, very poor for 25 days and severe for eight days.
In 2023, the city recorded one satisfactory day, 12 moderate days, 16 poor days, 17 very poor days and 10 severe days.
In 2022, there were two good days, four satisfactory days, eight moderate days, 22 poor days, 17 very poor days and three severe days.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 2022, there were two good days, four satisfactory days, eight moderate days, 22 poor days, 17 very poor days and three severe days.

articles.title: Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use, better mental health: study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants.
Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement.

Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use.

The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO).
Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression.
The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said.

Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad.

articles.title: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission . On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms.

The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support.

Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models.

On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models.

The government has also defended Sarvam’s commercial strategy. IT Secretary S Krishnan told reporters that the Centre did not see any misuse of IndiaAI Mission support in the company’s decision to offer foreign-developed models through Token Factory. “Based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support, which the IndiaAI Mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering,” he said. Krishnan said there was no contradiction between developing indigenous models and offering foreign-developed ones commercially, adding that AI companies also needed a revenue model.
Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API).

An API allows one software application to communicate with another. Instead of setting up and managing the infrastructure needed to run a model, a business can connect its software to Sarvam’s API and send requests to the model it wants to use.

The platform offers Sarvam’s 105-billion-parameter model, alongside open-weight models such as GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash from China’s Z.ai, DeepSeek V4 models from DeepSeek, Kimi models from Moonshot AI, and Google’s Gemma 4 31B.
Open-weight models are those whose trained parameters, or weights, are made available for others to download and run. Businesses can use them without having to develop the models from scratch.
Sarvam says Token Factory runs the models on GPU clusters located in India. Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed.

Training is the process of teaching an AI model using large amounts of data. Inference is the process of using a trained model to perform tasks such as answering questions, summarising documents, writing code or translating languages. For example, when a user asks a chatbot to summarise a report, the model uses what it learnt during training to generate a response. It does not need to be trained again for every request.

The two stages have different computing requirements. Training a large model from scratch requires enormous computing power over an extended period. Inference involves running the trained model repeatedly to answer user requests, often handling thousands of requests at the same time. The infrastructure must therefore deliver responses quickly and reliably.

articles.title: Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department
Frequent interactions between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals raise concerns about disease transmission to wildlife in the Nilgiris.

According to a report submitted by the Forest Department to the Madras High Court, five of the 12 reported instances of infections that caused wildlife deaths, likely due to interactions with feral animals, since 2005 were recorded in the Nilgiris district.
Necropsy on wildlife carcasses had found canine distemper and rabies as the cause of deaths, which had been reported in the Nilgiris, Gudalur and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) forest divisions.

S. Muralidharan, who is appearing as the party-in-person before the High Court, has sought judicial intervention to address the threat to wildlife. He told The Hindu that there have been instances of diseases such as canine distemper and rabies spreading to wildlife from free-ranging domestic animals, particularly dogs.

He pointed out that such diseases had threatened the survival of vulnerable wildlife populations, citing outbreaks of canine distemper among Asiatic lions in Gujarat as an example of the potential consequences. “This is a very serious concern, especially in areas where there is a very high interface between wildlife and human communities, which feed and maintain free-ranging dog populations, like in the Nilgiris” he said.

Mr. Muralidharan called on the government to take measures to manage free-ranging dogs and cats in areas bordering tiger reserves and reserve forests across the State, including their removal from these areas to protect wildlife.
“These animals also hunt small game such as birds and even deer and can be extremely aggressive,” he said.

According to the report filed by the Forest Department, the deaths of the 12 animals reported due to transmission of disease from domestic animals include those of leopards (canine distemper), Nilgiri langur (rabies), Indian gaur (rabies), sloth bear (rabies and ehrlichiosis) and golden jackals (canine distemper and parvovirus infection).

Conservationists said that the number of animals dying from diseases transmitted to wildlife from feral animals could be much higher as not all wildlife deaths are reported or are noticed if they occur inside reserve forests.

The deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, but the Nilgiris had the highest number of the reported deaths.
In Gudalur, two wildlife deaths — a leopard and a tiger — occurred due to canine distemper in 2026, according to Forest officials.

When contacted, P. Devaraj, Divisional Forest Officer, Gudalur Division, said dogs and cattle in villages around Mudumalai Tiger Reserve are vaccinated every year, and the practice has also been expanded to Gudalur as well in 2026.

articles.title: Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient in vitamin B12: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women

Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR).
The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women.

The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient.

The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL.

Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment.

“Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune.

He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions.

The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes.

Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.

The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.

Anura Kurpad, professor of Physiology and Nutrition, St. John’s Medical College, Bengaluru, noted that the high prevalence of vitamin B12 deficiency reported in SAMPADA needs to be interpreted with caution.

“The cut-offs currently used are not based on clinical health outcomes and may not accurately reflect B12 status in Indian populations, which habitually consume less of the vitamin. Importantly, SAMPADA found no higher prevalence of B12 deficiency among anaemic individuals, raising questions about its clinical significance. Before rushing into widespread supplementation or food fortification, India needs research to establish population-specific B12 cut-offs and evidence of actual health benefits. Otherwise, we risk creating a nutritional crisis based on laboratory numbers rather than disease,” he said.

articles.title: Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam

The Sthanika Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day.

The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon , it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules.

A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. They said they had given consent for lighting the lamp at the usual spot near Uchipillaiyar Temple “last year” (2025). The recent statement by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department referring to their consent, made “without consulting” them, had caused mental agony, they said.

Meanwhile, there was commotion outside the house of Swaminatha Bhattar late in the evening on Wednesday, as functionaries of the BJP and Hindu outfits arrived at the priest’s house. Temple officials too were present at the house. The BJP functionaries said the Bhattars were being “forced” to give a new letter of consent to help the officials substantiate their stand before the Supreme Court. The demonstrators were detained by the police.

An official of the Department said the Bhattars gave the new letter on Wednesday to the Board of Trustees. “The lighting of Karthigai Deepam has been done at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since 1996 with the cooperation of the temple authorities,” said the letter, signed by four Bhattars. However, they underlined that they were only replying to a letter written by the temple administration, seeking their opinion on this issue.

They reasoned that the Utchipillaiyar Temple, the Rajagopuram, and the venue for burning chokkapanai near the 16-Pillar Mandapam lie on a straight line, and the Utchipillaiyar Temple was located right above the sanctum sanctorum. They also confirmed that they had given the same opinion “in writing” on November 7, 2013 and December 4, 2025. “The deepam is lit at the deepamandapam after getting oral or written opinion from us every year. This is in line with the agama rules and age-old Saiva customs,” they clarified.

articles.title: GVMC receives 803 applications during three days tax melas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A total of 803 applications were received during the three-day Revenue Tax Melas organised by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) across its zones from November 24 to 26, Commissioner Ketan Garg said on Thursday.
The civic body received 93 applications on the first day, 394 on the second and 316 on the third.
Among the zones, the North Zone recorded the highest number of submissions at 159, followed by Madhurawada 103 and East Zone with 97. Aganampudi recorded the lowest, at 27.

According to Mr. Garg, requests for change of ownership accounted for the largest share with 229 applications, followed by 168 general revision petitions and 142 applications for new assessments. The corporation also received 87 applications for correction of house numbers, 38 for correction of owners’ names and 94 concerning other issues. The remaining applications were related to demolitions, assessment modifications, bifurcations, property tax exemptions and mergers.
Mr. Garg directed officials to scrutinise all applications and resolve the grievances promptly.

articles.title: Karnataka’s Escoms plan to pass profits to consumers via lower power bills from April 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a relief for electricity consumers amid rising household expenses, electricity supply companies (Escoms) across Karnataka are likely to pass on their profits to consumers in the form of a refund of around 16 paise per unit from April 2027.

Sources in the Energy Department said on Thursday that most Escoms, including Bangalore Electricity Supply Company (Bescom), Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company (Gescom), Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation (CESC), and Mangalore Electricity Supply Company (Mescom), have recorded profits for the financial year 2025-26. However, Hubli Electricity Supply Company (Hescom) is an exception.

A senior Energy Department official said the improved financial performance would enable Escoms to return the gains to consumers. Bescom alone reported a profit of ₹293.62 crore during 2025-26, while the profit figures of other Escoms are yet to be officially announced.

Every year, Escoms are required to submit their tariff status and profit-and-loss statements, known as truing-up petitions, to the Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) as part of their annual performance review. The companies are scheduled to submit their petitions on November 30.
Once the proposals receive KERC’s approval, the refund will be adjusted against electricity bills for consumption from April 2027.

While the average refund is expected to be around 16 paise per unit, consumers in some Escom jurisdictions could receive a higher benefit. Bescom sources said the company was seeking a refund of 35 paise per unit, although the proposal is yet to be finalised. The approved amount is expected to be announced on the Bescom website in December 2026.

Officials attributed the improved financial performance to a reduction in power distribution losses from 11% to around 9.13%. Escoms also reduced power procurement costs by utilising more electricity generated through hydropower instead of relying on relatively expensive thermal power.

articles.title: Workers of BJP, JD(S) stage protest opposing Operation Gaja at Kadabagere in Chikkamagaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Workers of the BJP and the JD(S) from Khandya hobli in Chikkamagaluru taluk jointly staged a protest at Kadabagere village on Thursday against Operation Gaja, the drive to push wild elephants from parts of Hassan district towards the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary.

The workers took out a protest march in the village and raised slogans against the State government and the Congress MLAs, alleging that they had failed to represent the farmers affected by the government’s decision. They described the operation, which seeks to drive the elephants to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, most of which lies in Chikkamagaluru district, as an unscientific move.

Former Minister D.N. Jeevaraj said the Forest Department should take responsibility for the crisis. “The plantations we have cultivated have become more comfortable habitats for elephants than the actual forest. The forest consists mostly of trees like acacia, which contribute little to its biodiversity. Hence, elephants find our plantations more suitable,” he said.

He also criticised the announcement by the Congress MLAs that they would resign, saying the legislators were only staging a drama instead of pressing the State government to protect the people of Chikkamagaluru from the elephant menace.

articles.title: Four-member gang targeting cab, bike taxi drivers arrested in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Gang allegedly committed over 30 robberies in three months to fund drug purchases; police trace 11 cases

The Whitefield police have busted an extortion racket and arrested four men who allegedly targeted cab and bike taxi drivers at night, assaulted them, and extorted money. The gang is suspected of having committed over two dozen such robberies in the past three months to fund their drug addiction and other vices.
The accused have been identified as Manoj, Preetham Prakash, Syed Shafi, and Akhilesh, residents of Gandhipura and Vijayanagar in Whitefield.

The arrests followed a complaint by Mohammed Nisar, a bike rider, who was allegedly intercepted and assaulted by the accused on an isolated stretch near Nallurhalli Metro station. The accused, who arrived in a car, allegedly assaulted him and forced him to transfer money online from his mobile phone before fleeing.
Following the complaint, a team of Whitefield police, led by DCP Haribabu, launched an operation to track down the gang.

The police traced the rental aggregator through which the accused had hired the car and followed the vehicle for around 2 km to 3 km. As the accused allegedly drove at high speed to evade the police, the investigators sought the rental company’s assistance in remotely switching off the car’s engine.

When the vehicle came to a halt, the accused stepped out to check the engine. Police personnel surrounded the car and arrested three of them on the spot. The fourth accused, who initially managed to escape, was arrested later.

The probe revealed that all four accused were drug users and allegedly committed the robberies to raise money to buy narcotics. The money extorted from drivers was reportedly transferred directly to the bank account of a suspected drug peddler.

Manoj, the prime accused, allegedly planned the robberies and identified potential targets. Preetham Prakash, a BCom graduate, was his associate, while Syed Shafi worked as a cab driver and Akhilesh was employed as a tattoo artist.
The gang initially used an autorickshaw to commit the robberies but later switched to a rented car to target drivers.
During interrogation, the accused allegedly confessed to committing around 30 robberies in three months. The police have so far traced and linked the gang to 11 incidents.
Investigators are also identifying other victims, as several drivers who lost relatively small amounts of money had not approached the police to file complaints.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 26 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Four-member gang targeting cab, bike taxi drivers arrested in Bengaluru

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Gang allegedly committed over 30 robberies in three months to fund drug purchases; police trace 11 cases

The Whitefield police have busted an extortion racket and arrested four men who allegedly targeted cab and bike taxi drivers at night, assaulted them, and extorted money. The gang is suspected of having committed over two dozen such robberies in the past three months to fund their drug addiction and other vices.

The accused have been identified as Manoj, Preetham Prakash, Syed Shafi, and Akhilesh, residents of Gandhipura and Vijayanagar in Whitefield.

The arrests followed a complaint by Mohammed Nisar, a bike rider, who was allegedly intercepted and assaulted by the accused on an isolated stretch near Nallurhalli Metro station. The accused, who arrived in a car, allegedly assaulted him and forced him to transfer money online from his mobile phone before fleeing.

Following the complaint, a team of Whitefield police, led by DCP Haribabu, launched an operation to track down the gang.

The police traced the rental aggregator through which the accused had hired the car and followed the vehicle for around 2 km to 3 km. As the accused allegedly drove at high speed to evade the police, the investigators sought the rental company’s assistance in remotely switching off the car’s engine.

When the vehicle came to a halt, the accused stepped out to check the engine. Police personnel surrounded the car and arrested three of them on the spot. The fourth accused, who initially managed to escape, was arrested later.

The probe revealed that all four accused were drug users and allegedly committed the robberies to raise money to buy narcotics. The money extorted from drivers was reportedly transferred directly to the bank account of a suspected drug peddler.

Manoj, the prime accused, allegedly planned the robberies and identified potential targets. Preetham Prakash, a BCom graduate, was his associate, while Syed Shafi worked as a cab driver and Akhilesh was employed as a tattoo artist.

The gang initially used an autorickshaw to commit the robberies but later switched to a rented car to target drivers.

During interrogation, the accused allegedly confessed to committing around 30 robberies in three months. The police have so far traced and linked the gang to 11 incidents.

Investigators are also identifying other victims, as several drivers who lost relatively small amounts of money had not approached the police to file complaints.

The gang is suspected of having committed over two dozen such robberies in the past three months to fund their drug addiction and other vices.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Investigators are also identifying other victims, as several drivers who lost relatively small amounts of money had not approached the police to file complaints.

articles.title: CPI announces three-day ‘Jail Bharo Andolan’ from December 1
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Demands include CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, implementation of women’s quota, and legal MSP guarantee for farmers

Communist Party of India (CPI) general secretary D. Raja on Thursday (November 26, 2026) announced a three-day “Jail Bharo Andolan” from December 1 to 3 on a set of political and economic demands, including the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, implementation of women’s reservation, and a legal guarantee for Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Raja said the country was facing multiple crises, claiming that the economy was in a poor state, prices were rising and unemployment remained high. He also expressed concern over “increasing atrocities against minorities, Dalits, women and children.”

The CPI leader said Prime Minister Narendra Modi often spoke and wrote about the Constitution but he should be “truthful to the people and the country”. He said the Constitution made it clear that India should remain a secular democratic republic and noted that B.R. Ambedkar had rejected the idea of a theocratic state. Mr. Raja accused Mr. Modi of seeking to establish a “Hindu Rashtra”, which he described as a “unidimensional, monolithic neoliberal medieval social order” that perpetuated caste inequalities and subverted the Constitution.
Mr. Raja appealed to “all secular democratic forces” to unite against the BJP and work towards defeating the ruling party in the coming Assembly elections in five States.
He said the CPI had held informal discussions with the Samajwadi Party and the Congress regarding seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war
Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territory held by the Iran-backed group including the capital Sanaa on Thursday (November 26, 2026), hours after it struck Riyadh.
The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war, which first began more than a decade ago.

The coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said during the night that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital of Riyadh, where residents and an AFP journalist heard an explosion.
It also said it had destroyed a cruise missile launched towards the west of the country and a drone in the Jeddah region on the Red Sea.
"The air force of the Saudi enemy today launched a series of strikes at the capital Sanaa," the Houthis' press agency reported on Thursday morning.
An AFP journalist in Sanaa reported seeing smoke in the area of the airport. The Houthi news outlet Almasirah reported that the strikes targeted a factory and warehouses in Bani al-Harith.
Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), residents of the key Houthi-controlled port of Hodeida told AFP they had heard jets flying over the city and loud explosions.
Almasirah said the strikes destroyed a wastewater treatment facility serving a densely populated district.
The Houthis said the day before they had struck two Saudi ports on the Red Sea, after Saudi strikes on Hodeida.
The coalition, meanwhile, said it had brought down a Houthi projectile targeting Jazan that had caused light damage and no civilian casualties.
Yemen's civil war burst back into life in July, bringing to an end a years-long truce that began in 2022.
The fighting has intensified since September, with the Houthis making significant territorial gains and bearing down on the temporary seat of the government in Aden.

articles.title: Israel kills nine in Gaza, including Hamas-appointed deputy Education Minister, officials say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the Deputy Gaza Education Minister, and his wife.

Israeli airstrikes ‌and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians overnight, medics said, including the ​Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education in the Gaza Strip, in ⁠a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-old ceasefire.
Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of ‌a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and ‌senior ⁠officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 ⁠Hamas militants in the past month.
"No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us," said Mr. Netanyahu.

The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw ​Hamas' economic portfolio and managed its ‌banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup. The military said his death may weaken the group's ability to sustain its finances and support its military capabilities. Hamas confirmed the death but had ‌no immediate comment on the allegations about his role.

Two other separate ​airstrikes killed six people in Tuffah neighbourhood and Beach refugee camp overnight in Gaza City, medics added. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), ⁠medics said Israeli gunfire killed a 62-year-old man in eastern Bureij refugee camp.
The Israeli military didn't immediately comment on those seven reported deaths.

Israel has continued to ‌carry out attacks that it says target Hamas but which have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas' disarmament.
Abu Nada was the third senior Hamas official Israel has killed since Tuesday, after two senior security officials.
At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed ‌since the ceasefire was agreed in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.
Israeli ​troops now control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling ⁠a sliver of territory along Gaza's coast.

Israel's assault on Gaza has killed ⁠more than 74,000 Palestinians since 2023, caused a hunger crisis, internally displaced Gaza's entire population and led to assessments of genocide from scholars ‌and a United Nations inquiry.

articles.title: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian nations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia

U.S. tech titan Nvidia is not allowing orders of computer servers containing its artificial intelligence chips to be shipped to four Southeast Asian countries, the Financial Times reported Thursday (November 26, 2026).

The article comes after Washington tightened export controls for the sensitive components in the wake of an espionage scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, forcing out longtime CEO Jensen Huang before his reinstatement on Sunday (November 22, 2026).
Citing national security concerns, the United States has since 2022 restricted export to tech rival China of Nvidia's industry-leading advanced chips that are used to train and run AI tools.

Washington last week moved to close a loophole in those controls, to crack down on chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries, often in Southeast Asia.
The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
The British newspaper, citing three people with knowledge of the matter, said it was unclear whether the halt was temporary.
What are AI PCs that Nvidia's Jensen Huang is betting on?
Nvidia's web of AI bets: smart strategy or bubble risk?
It named U.S. giants Dell and Supermicro, who package Nvidia AI chips into servers for data centres, as two affected partners.

Buyers affected include Singapore-based cloud computing company Aolani, which had planned to provide access to the Nvidia hardware to Chinese TikTok owner ByteDance through leasing agreements, the Financial Times said.
An executive at a cloud provider told the newspaper that Washington's new rules had caused "sheer chaos" in the region during a 90-day period in which to apply for a newly required licence.
AFP has contacted Nvidia, Dell, Supermicro, Aolani and ByteDance for comment.

articles.title: Kremlin accuses Ukraine of trying to widen conflict zone to Mediterranean and Baltic seas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, a day after ​it carried out a ‌drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland
The Kremlin on Thursday (November 26, 2026) accused Ukraine of trying to spread ​the war it is fighting against Russia to the Mediterranean ‌and Baltics seas, a move it called very dangerous.

U.S. ​President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark ⁠Rutte said in a joint statement on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after a meeting in Florida that Russia should avoid actions that expand its full-scale ‌war in Ukraine, which it launched in 2022. Their intervention appeared to be a warning to Moscow ‌to think twice about how it retaliated against ‌Ukraine ⁠over recent attacks Kyiv has launched on Russian interests ⁠far from the conflict zone.
Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, a day after ​it carried out a ‌drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland.

Responding to the joint U.S.-NATO statement, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that nobody wanted the conflict ‌to expand, but he said Ukraine, not Russia was ​the one trying to widen the area of conflict.

"As regards the escalation of the conflict in ⁠Ukraine, this appears to refer to attempts by the Kyiv regime to expand the geographical scope of this conflict. We ‌are witnessing terrorist activity by the Kyiv regime in the Mediterranean and the Baltic," Mr. Peskov told reporters on a conference call.

articles.title: Myanmar says it will not fully comply with ICJ genocide orders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it

Myanmar's military-backed ‌President has said his administration will not comply with all ​measures ordered by the UN's top court, which last ⁠week ruled that the country's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) found that the Myanmar military's actions against the mainly ‌Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, including thousands of killings, the burning of hundreds of villages and widespread sexual violence, amounted ‌to genocide — and ordered a slew of measures.
The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it.
"Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," he said in a meeting on ‌Wednesday, according to state media.
Min Aung Hlaing did not elaborate ​on what court orders his administration considered inappropriate.

The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to end ongoing breaches of the Genocide ⁠Convention and promptly investigate, prosecute and punish people reasonably suspected of involvement in the 2017 military operations. It also ordered the country to provide guarantees ‌that such violations will not be repeated.

Myanmar must also facilitate the return of displaced Rohingya, restore or replace lost property, help locate missing people, provide rehabilitation to survivors, and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution.
The court further ordered Myanmar to pay compensation for the harm caused to Rohingya that is not remedied through restitution.
Myanmar must report ‌back within two years on the measures it has taken, including proposed compensation, ​the order said.
Myanmar has maintained that operations undertaken by its security forces in northern Rakhine state during 2016–2018 ⁠were counter-terrorism actions against an insurgent group.
The country's foreign ministry has previously ⁠said that operations were "not carried out with genocidal intent but instead were limited in scope and duration, lasting only a matter of ‌days."
The 2017 military crackdown drove more than 730,000 Rohingya from Rakhine state into neighbouring Bangladesh, where the refugee population in sprawling ​camps has now swelled to about 1.2 million.

articles.title: China's Defence Ministry urges Japan to stop 'stirring up' South China Sea disputes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The comments were in response to an ⁠announcement earlier this month that Japan will provide the Philippines with radars and drones to boost its coastal surveillance capabilities

China's Defence Ministry urged Japan on Thursday (November 26, 2026) to stop "stirring up ​trouble" over the South China Sea after a spokesperson was asked about ‌deepening cooperation between Tokyo and the Philippines, both formal ​U.S. military allies.
Chinese and Philippine coastguard vessels ‌frequently clash near disputed shoals and reefs as part of long-simmering tensions over the vital trade waterway.
Defence Ministry ‌spokesperson Chen Xi told a regular press briefing in Beijing ‌that ⁠Japan was not party to the disputes and had ⁠no right to comment on them.
"We demand that Japan stop stirring up trouble over the South China Sea issue," Mr. Chen Xi said.
Japan had used "so-called external threats" ​to deepen regional anxieties, form military ‌cliques and attempt to strengthen its military presence in the South China Sea, he added.

The U.S. and its allies and partners have repeatedly expressed concern over the situation in the South ‌China Sea as China asserts its sovereignty through growing deployments ​of naval, coastguard and militia vessels.

China claims nearly all of the South China Sea, overlapping maritime claims of ⁠the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan. In 2016, a Hague-based tribunal said China's claims had no legal basis, a decision Beijing ‌has rejected.
China's Military is also operating further out into the Pacific and is present on a daily basis around Taiwan, which Beijing views as its own territory.

China carried out a large, unannounced military exercise across the western Pacific and around Taiwan in early November, in what officials in Taipei have previously described ‌as a campaign of "silent intimidation".

Mr. Chen Xi, asked about those drills, said the Military's stepped-up training ​and combat readiness, and its continuous improvement of practical capabilities to defend China's sovereignty and territorial integrity, are "entirely legitimate and ⁠reasonable".
"We oppose certain parties hyping it up with ulterior motives," he ⁠added.
"The Democratic Progressive Party authorities are the biggest disruptors of the status quo in the Taiwan Strait," Chen said, ‌referring to Taiwan's ruling party.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The government must build consensus on delimitation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) appears to have zeroed in on a hurried delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies as the central piece of its strategy for the next general election, due in 2029. As the current constitutional scheme stands, a fresh delimitation is triggered once the data from the ongoing Census 2027 is published . That default path, which is based on population distribution across States, will considerably cut down the representation of States that have stabilised their population since the last delimitation. The Centre has now proposed to extend the constitutional freeze on inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, while increasing the size of the House to a maximum of 850 seats. The demarcation of the boundaries of Lok Sabha constituencies will be based on the 2011 Census within each State. The delimitation exercise will also bring into force 33% reservation for women , which Parliament approved in 2023. Considering the need to balance the ‘one person, one vote’ principle with the principles of federalism, which is about protecting the group rights of States, the proposals are a reasonable way forward for India. That said, the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats is such a central question of democracy and federalism that any changes must be preceded by thoughtful deliberations at multiple levels.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bharatiya Janata Party / Delimitation / Lok Sabha / election / Census 2027 / population / parliament / India / political parties / Women's Representation

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Science-based diplomacy could aid India-Pakistan bilateral engagement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The economic and diplomatic consequences of India’s efforts to estrange Pakistan often overshadow the costs distributed between them. For example, Pakistani space scientists can today access facilities in China whereas Indian space scientists can access facilities in the United States and Europe . But Indian scientists studying environmental conditions in Pakistan and Pakistani scientists studying conditions in India have far fewer alternatives. The latter matters much more for regional development and stability. On November 25, Beijing’s ‘Space Silk Road’ diplomacy and the strain on New Delhi’s hedging strategies converged in the Shenzhou-24 mission as China launched Pakistan’s first astronaut , Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to the Tiangong space station. Pakistan had offered in 2015 to contribute to India’s proposed SAARC satellite and wanted the project administered under SAARC, but India insisted on operating it as largesse to its neighbours. If it had really been SAARC’s satellite, ISRO and its Pakistani counterpart, SUPARCO , could have developed an institutional relationship and India could have influenced its neighbour’s space programme through a multilateral mechanism. But today, India’s ability to engage Pakistan on regional matters has increasingly depended on negotiating with powers beyond South Asia, in institutions with other agendas.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Pakistan / China / space programme / USA / European / SAARC / ISRO / Asia / Bangladesh / Belt and Road Initiative / Balakot Air Strikes / diplomacy

Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Punjab / voting / Indian National Congress / General Elections 2024 / Shiromani Akali Dal / Aam Aadmi Party / agriculture / economy / welfare
